docs.text: Two loggers, two clocks, two naming habits: --align auto lines the run up with the golden run by cross-correlation (--align-on NAME to choose the signal, --align SECONDS to give the shift), names match with or without their unit, and {"as": "name in the run"} in the tolerances pairs signals named differently. A worked example: Simulation against flight.

docs.title: A run envelope's results: sweep
docs.text:
signalviewer-cli sweep results.csv --question question.json         # how many sets hold, the best five
signalviewer-cli sweep results/ --question study.svsweep --top 10   # a folder of tables; a study saved by the app
signalviewer-cli sweep results.csv --question q.json --min-holding 3 --json

{"conditions": [{"column": "roll_error_deg", "op": "<=", "value": 5, "mode": "all"},
                {"column": "overshoot_pct", "op": "<=", "value": 15, "mode": "all"}],
 "combine": "and", "goal": {"column": "energy_wh", "direction": "min"}}

The table has a row per run (CSV, Parquet or Excel, or a folder of them); the columns' roles are guessed as in the app's Sweeps area, and a study saved there (.svsweep) brings its own roles and goal. The answer is the app's: how many parameter sets meet every condition in every must-hold-across combination, and the best of them. On the bundled example (examples/sweeps/drone_tuning.csv):

12 of 45 parameter sets hold in all 18 combinations (0 miss a combination)
  roll_error_deg <= 5: met by 27
  overshoot_pct <= 15: met by 28
  1. kp_roll=0.2, ki_roll=0.02, filter_hz=10, goal=47.86

Exit code 0 = at least --min-holding sets hold (default 1), 1 = fewer, 2 = the table or the question cannot be read - so a CI job fails when a change leaves no tuning that works everywhere.

docs.title: Numerical validation: validate
docs.text:
signalviewer-cli validate                   # one line per case, then "23 passed, 0 failed"
signalviewer-cli validate --json            # every case with expected, measured, error, tolerance
signalviewer-cli validate --junit v.xml     # JUnit XML, e.g. as a record that this installation computes correctly

Spectra, filters, derivative and integral, statistics, decimation, Compare and coordinate frames, each against a reference that does not come from the app. Exit code 0 = every case within its tolerance, 1 = one is not. The cases and the conventions behind them: Validation.

docs.title: Map objects: objects, compare-objects, compare-similar, map
docs.text:
The objects a file holds - found by their names with the app's rules (one table, backend/svcore/object_names.json) - and their comparison, with the same numbers as the app's Compare objects… dialog. The whole process with Python, the command line and REST, step by step: API.

signalviewer-cli objects flight.bin                 # POS: navigation (POS), LLA ... XKF1[1]: NED, origin ORGN[0] (known)
signalviewer-cli objects flight.bin --all --json    # also what Add all would not add; the reasons as data
signalviewer-cli compare-objects flight.bin --ref POS --objects "XKF1[0],XKF1[1]" \
    --what position,velocity,attitude --frame ned \
    --csv errors.csv --stats stats.csv --map map.png --map-html map.html --report report.html
signalviewer-cli compare-objects flight.bin --ref POS --tolerance position=2m,attitude=1deg --junit r.xml   # CI
signalviewer-cli compare-objects truth.csv flight.bin --ref truth:phys --objects POS   # two files
signalviewer-cli compare-similar flight.bin --leaf Yaw --ref "XKF1[0]" --csv yaw.csv   # nav1 / nav2, XKF1[0] / XKF1[1]
signalviewer-cli map flight.bin --out map.html      # the offline map page (or .png / .svg)

compare-objects: --frame is ned, enu, ecef, lla (north / east / up) or track (along / cross / up). Each object's errors against the reference: the differences per component, the horizontal / vertical / 3D error, the velocity differences and the speed error, the roll / pitch / yaw errors (yaw wrapped to ±180°), and their statistics on the full data (RMS, mean, largest |error| and when, 95th percentile). Quantities that cannot be compared (no velocity, no attitude of its own) are left out and named. With --tolerance, every error component of a quantity must stay within it (its largest |error|): exit code 0 = all within, 1 = one is not, 2 = it could not be compared; --junit writes one test case per object and quantity.

Several files: the objects of each, an object named file:name where two files share a name; each on its own recorded time (no offset), the compared object read onto the reference's samples (linear) - as the app.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
import signalviewer as sv
rec = sv.load("flight.bin")
t, roll = rec.signal("ATT.Roll")
df = rec.to_dataframe(["ATT.Roll", "ATT.Pitch"], t0=10, t1=60)     # one time base
sv.show(t, {"roll x2": 2 * roll}, name="from my notebook")         # into the open app

rec.objects()                                    # the map objects: name, class, frame, origin, why
nav = rec.object("XKF1[0]")                      # t, lat, lon, alt (NED placed on Earth), roll, pitch, yaw, vn, ve, vd
cmp = sv.compare_objects(rec, reference="POS", objects=["XKF1[0]", "XKF1[1]"], what=("position", "attitude"))
cmp.stats()                                      # object x component -> rms, mean, max_abs, p95_abs, t_max_abs
cmp.errors(); cmp.values(); cmp.to_csv("errors.csv"); cmp.to_mat("errors.mat")
sv.similar(rec)                                  # families of similar signals
sv.compare_signals(rec, ["XKF1[1].Yaw [deg]"], reference="XKF1[0].Yaw [deg]")   # angles wrapped
sv.map_image(rec, path="map.png"); sv.map_html(rec, path="map.html")
sv.report(rec, "report.pdf", compare=cmp)        # the map, the error plots, the statistics table

docs.title: Your own formats
docs.text:
signalviewer-cli readers shows the readers folder (~/.signalviewer/readers) and what is in it; readers --example writes a Python reader to start from:

@reader(extensions=[".kv"], name="key=value lines")
def read_kv(path):
    ...
    return {"time": t, "signals": {"speed": speed, "mode": codes}, "labels": {"mode": {0: "IDLE", 1: "RUN"}}}

Return one time for all signals, or a tuple (time, values) for a signal with its own time, or None for "not my file". Saving the file is enough - no restart.

docs.title: Raw binary packets (ICD layouts)
docs.text:
A <name>.icd.json in the readers folder describes packets as they come off the wire; files with its extensions then open as signals <packet>.<field> [unit]. Try it with signalviewer-cli readers --example-icd run.tlm (a layout and a recording).

{"name": "Bench telemetry", "extensions": [".tlm"], "byte_order": "little",
 "header": {"sync": "0xA55A", "size": 4, "id": {"offset": 2, "type": "u8"}, "length": {"offset": 3, "type": "u8"}},
 "packets": [{"id": 1, "name": "NAV", "size": 14, "time": "t_us", "time_scale": 1e-6, "fields": [
   {"name": "t_us", "offset": 0, "type": "u32"},
   {"name": "alt", "offset": 4, "type": "i32", "scale": 0.01, "unit": "m"},
   {"name": "mode", "offset": 10, "type": "u8", "enum": {"0": "IDLE", "1": "CLIMB", "2": "CRUISE"}},
   {"name": "armed", "offset": 11, "type": "u8", "bits": [0, 1]},
   {"name": "volt", "offset": 12, "type": "u16", "scale": 0.001, "unit": "V", "byte_order": "big"}]}]}

Types u8 i8 u16 i16 u32 i32 u64 i64 f32 f64; value = raw × scale + offset_value. Time from a packet's field, else from the header ("time": {"offset", "type", "scale"}), else the packets are numbered. Noise, unknown ids and a cut-off end are skipped to the next sync and counted in the load report. YAML layouts (.icd.yaml) work when PyYAML is installed.

docs.title: CAN bus logs
docs.text: candump logs (.log), Vector ASC (.asc) and CAN frame tables (.csv with time, id and data columns) open with every .dbc next to the log or in the readers folder. Signals are named <Message>.<Signal> [unit], each message at its own rate; value names become text values. Multiplexed signals, float signals, 29-bit ids and CAN FD payloads are decoded; frames whose id is in no .dbc are counted in the load report.

docs.title: With pip: full or light
docs.text: pip install signalviewer has everything. pip install signalviewer-lite is the core (CSV, MATLAB v5, ArduPilot .bin, CAN, binary layouts, every plot and analysis, HTML reports); its extras: [parquet] [hdf5] (.h5, MATLAB v7.3) [mavlink] (.tlog, live) [px4] (.ulg) [ros] (.mcap) [reports] (PDF, Word, images) [desktop] - or [all]. A file that needs a missing extra says which. Install one of the two packages, not both (they install the same signalviewer module).

docs.title: סט פרמטרים אחד לכמה מערכות
docs.text: Sweeps ← פתיחה ▾ ← מחקר חדש… ← יש לי תוצאות, ואז מוסיפים את הטבלה של כל מערכת (בנווט של המחקר). הרצתם סריקה לכל אחת מכמה מערכות - למשל שלושה רחפנים - וכולן חייבות לטוס עם אותם הגברים. לכל טבלה תרחישים משלה (רוח, מסה), מגבלות משלה ויעד משלה. Signal Viewer מוצא את ערכי הפרמטרים המשותפים שעומדים בדרישות בכל הטבלאות, ומדרג אותם – בפריט ביחד של הנווט, שמופיע כשיש במחקר שתי טבלאות או יותר (מחקר עם טבלה אחת מדורג בפני עצמו).

docs.title: השאלה - בקובץ מחקר
docs.text:
מחקר (<name>.svstudy.json) נבנה באפליקציה – בהגדרה שבנווט – ונשמר במחקר ▾ ← שמירה; פתיחת מחקר שמור פותח אותו שוב, ואותו קובץ נקרא גם משורת הפקודה.

עמודה היא… משמעות דוגמה משותפת קיימת בכל הטבלאות (אחרי התאמת שמות). נבחר ערך אחד לכולן. Kp, Ki, Kd תרחיש בטבלה הזאת בלבד. הבחירה חייבת לעמוד בכל ערך שנשאר. רוח, מסה מקומית בטבלה הזאת בלבד. כל טבלה בוחרת לעצמה את הערך הטוב. מסנן תוצאה תוצאת ההרצה. overshoot, זמן התייצבות
  • שמות: P_gain בטבלה אחת ו-Kp באחרת מוצעים כשם אחד; אתם מאשרים.
  • לכל טבלה: ערכי התרחישים שנחשבים, האילוצים (overshoot < 8), היעד (להקטין את settling_time) ואיך מצרפים תרחישים - המקרה הגרוע (ברירת מחדל) או הממוצע.
  • טבלאות הן נתיבים או תבניות ליד קובץ המחקר: קובץ תוצאות חדש בתיקייה נקרא בפתיחה הבאה.

docs.title: התשובה
docs.text:
לכל ערך של הפרמטרים המשותפים שהורץ:

  1. הוא עומד בטבלה כשיש ערך מקומי שבו ההרצה של כל תרחיש קיימת ועומדת באילוצים (הרצה חסרה נחשבת כישלון: לא הורץ);
  2. הציון שלו בטבלה הוא היעד הגרוע (או הממוצע) על פני התרחישים, עם הערך המקומי הטוב;
  3. הוא עומד בכולן כשהוא עומד בכל טבלה.

כשליעד זהה בכל הטבלאות - הדירוג לפי הטבלה הגרועה; כשהיעדים שונים - לפי חזית פארטו (אין ערך אחר טוב יותר בכל הטבלאות). ערך שנפסל אומר באיזו טבלה, באיזה תרחיש ובאיזה אילוץ נכשל, ובכמה. נבחרים רק ערכים שהורצו - כדי לנסות חדשים, מריצים את הסבב הבא מעמודת הרצה. ייצוא CSV… בביחד כותב את כל הדירוג; מחקר ▾ ← דוח של המחקר… כותב ממנו דף HTML אחד (היעד והמגבלות של כל טבלה, התשובה המשותפת עם הפסיקה של כל טבלה, הסבבים שהורצו).

docs.title: ההרצות הבאות
docs.text:
עמודת הרצה בצד המחקר אומרת מה הסבב הבא יריץ, או מה עוד חסר לו. הסבב הבא הוא מנה של 20 ערכים מועמדים (גודל המנה) של הפרמטרים המשותפים, כל אחד מורחב להרצות שלו בכל טבלה (התרחישים × הערכים המקומיים) - כך שמנה היא כמה מאות הרצות. להריץ אותן מריץ אותה (על ה-workers של המחשב הזה או דרך ה-launcher של החווה); רק לכתוב את הקבצים רק כותב אותה ל-launcher משלכם. לכל הרצה סיבה:

  • חידוד - סביב הערכים הטובים, בחצי מהצעד המקומי;
  • גבול - בין ערך שעומד לשכן שנכשל;
  • פער - ערכים שהורצו בחלק מהטבלאות ולא באחרות.

ההצעות נשארות בתוך מרחב החיפוש של המחקר ונכתבות ל-next/round_<k>/<table>.csv עם העמודות run_id, reason ו-round. הצעה שעדיין ממתינה לא מוצעת שוב; כשהתוצאות חוזרות עם ה-run_id (או אותם ערכים) היא מסומנת כבוצעה.

docs.title: שורת הפקודה
docs.text:
python -m signalviewer.study rank   drones.svstudy.json [--csv ranking.csv] [--json]
python -m signalviewer.study next   drones.svstudy.json          # כותב את הסבב; קוד יציאה 3 = לא נשאר מה להציע
python -m signalviewer.study status drones.svstudy.json

SignalViewer.exe study … עושה אותו דבר מהגרסה הניידת.

docs.title: הדוגמה
docs.text: מסך הפתיחה ← סט הגברים אחד לשלושה רחפנים (examples/drones/): קוואד קל, הקסה כבד ו-VTOL שהעמודות שלו נקראות P_gain, I_gain, D_gain, עם מסנן מקומי וכמה הרצות חסרות.

docs.title: One parameter set for many systems
docs.text: Sweeps → Open ▾ → New study… → I have results, then add each system's table (Add table in the Data step). You have run a sweep for each of several systems - three drones, say - and they must all fly with the same gains. Each table has its own scenarios (wind, mass), its own limits and its own goal. Signal Viewer finds the values of the shared parameters that hold in every table, and ranks them - the Results tab All systems together, shown when the study has two tables or more (a study with one table is ranked on its own).

docs.title: The question, in a study file
docs.text:
A study (<name>.svstudy.json) is built in the app - Send runs in the Data step, the goal in its tables' Goal step - and saved with Study ▾ → Save; Open a saved study opens it again, and the same file is read by the command line.

A column is… Meaning Example Shared In every table (after the names are paired). One value is chosen for all. Kp, Ki, Kd Scenario This table only. The choice must hold for every value of it you keep. wind, mass Local This table only. Each table picks its own best value. a filter Output A result of the run. overshoot, settling time
  • Names: P_gain in one table and Kp in another are proposed as one name; you confirm.
  • Per table: the scenario values that count, the constraints (overshoot < 8), the goal (minimise settling_time), and how scenarios combine - the worst case (default) or the mean.
  • Tables are paths or globs next to the study: a new results file in the folder is read on the next open.

docs.title: The answer
docs.text:
For each value of the shared parameters that was run:

  1. it holds in a table when some local value makes every scenario's run exist and meet the constraints (a missing run counts as a failure: not run);
  2. its score in that table is the worst (or mean) goal over the scenarios, with the best local value;
  3. it holds for all when it holds in every table.

With the same goal in every table, the values are ranked by the worst table; with different goals they are ranked on the Pareto front (no other value is better in every table). A rejected value says which table, scenario and constraint failed, and by how much. Only values that were run are chosen - to try new ones, run the next round from the Next runs step (Run from the app). Export CSV… in the systems together writes the whole ranking; Study ▾ → Report of the study… writes one HTML page of it (each table's goal and limits, the shared answer with each table's verdict, the rounds run).

docs.title: Next runs to try
docs.text:
The Run column on the right of the study says what the next round will run, or what is still missing for it. The next round is a batch of 20 candidate values (the batch size) of the shared parameters, each expanded to its runs in every table (its scenarios × local values) - so a batch is a few hundred runs. Run them runs it (on this PC's workers or through your farm's launcher); Only write the files only writes it for a launcher of your own. Each run has a reason:

  • refine - around the best values, at half the local step;
  • boundary - between a value that holds and a neighbour that fails;
  • gap - values run in some tables but not in others.

Proposals stay inside the study's search space (bounds, smallest step, allowed values, constraints on the shared parameters themselves) and are written to next/round_<k>/<table>.csv with a run_id, reason and round column. A proposal still pending is never proposed again; when results come back with the run_id (or the same values) it is marked done.

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
python -m signalviewer.study rank   drones.svstudy.json [--csv ranking.csv] [--json]
python -m signalviewer.study next   drones.svstudy.json          # writes the round; exit 3 = nothing left
python -m signalviewer.study status drones.svstudy.json

SignalViewer.exe study … does the same from the Portable. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 3 nothing left to propose at the smallest step.

docs.title: The example
docs.text: Welcome → One gain set for three drones (examples/drones/, made by tools/make_drone_sweeps.py from a toy attitude-loop model): a light quad (wind; overshoot < 8; fastest settling), a heavy hexa (mass × wind; overshoot < 12 and motor saturation < 0.9; least energy) and a VTOL whose columns are called P_gain, I_gain, D_gain, with a local filter and a few runs missing.

docs.title: Tests: numbers and real logs
docs.text:
The frontend's logic (cd frontend && npm test): Vitest unit tests next to the code they test (src/**/*.test.ts) - the workspace's commit / undo / redo, opening old sessions (files.ts), which signals the work uses (sameWork.ts), pairing signals with plots, the plot colours' contrast, the judge-a-run verdict, trust badges and the data-quality words. They run in Node without a browser (a few browser globals are stubbed in src/test/setup.ts); the screens are tested by tests/e2e.

cd backend && python -m pytest -q runs everything that needs no network, including the numerical validation (tests/test_validation.py; after changing a case, rewrite the page with python tools/make_validation_doc.py).

Real flight logs (tests/test_real_logs.py): logs recorded by real vehicles, not only the ones our own tools write, checked against their projects' own readers - ArduPilot DataFlash against pymavlink's DFReader (every numeric field), .tlog against pymavlink (every sample, on the autopilot's clock), PX4 .ulg against pyulog (every field of every topic) - and for invariants (finite, non-decreasing time; the health check runs). The public logs are pinned to a commit and a SHA-256 and kept outside the repository (their licences differ from ours):

python tools/fetch_real_logs.py                          # once: ~/.cache/signalviewer-test-logs
cd backend && python -m pytest -q tests/test_real_logs.py
SV_REAL_LOGS=/path/to/your/logs python -m pytest -q tests/test_real_logs.py   # your own logs too

Without the download those tests are skipped; the regression test for radio delay always runs.

docs.title: Welcome screen
docs.text:
• Recent files and recent sessions, one click to reopen; missing ones are marked and can be forgotten
  • Five examples in one click: a drone flight, the same mission flown twice, three car runs to compare, an ArduPilot flight log, a simulation against its flight (offered only when all their files are there)
  • An example opens with its view already applied (Undo: an empty plot)

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• The file dialog sorts by last modified (newest first, the default) or by name, with a date column
  • A file dragged in opens from its original (desktop window: the real path; otherwise found by name + size + modified time, one exact match only), so refresh and live mode follow it; only when it cannot be found is a copy used (marked "copy", with Choose the original file…)
  • CSV (auto-detect delimiter/header/time column, Excel BOM, text columns skipped, unsorted time sorted) and MATLAB .mat v5 / v7.3
  • Built-in file browser
  • Drag & drop onto the window
  • Import options with live preview
  • Load report after opening (what was skipped and why)
  • Rename, description, reload, replace with another file (plots keep their signals)
  • Time offset per file (badge in the list)
  • Link plots: a signal is added to and removed from the plot together with the same signal of every other file - signals made from it too (toggle in the file panel, saved with the workspace)
  • Link operations, on its own: a change on a signal (ƒ) - set, stacked or removed - or a new signal made from it (Create signals, Create signal ▸) is made on the same signal of every other file; with Link plots on, the new ones join the original's plots (toggle in the file panel, saved with the workspace)
  • Opening a file does not plot anything until you choose
  • Damaged files (cut off by a power loss, bad bytes, a block of zeros) open with what is still readable, with a note; a .mat cut off while MATLAB saved it keeps every complete variable
  • In the file dialog Shift+click selects a range and Ctrl+A every file shown; each use (open files, save a session, a report, an image) keeps its own last folder, and a first save starts where the data is
  • Opening a file that is already open reads it again from the disk (Open another copy on request)
  • Several files opened together: the start card suggests Compare open files
  • The timeline maps the recording: the active plot's first line drawn faintly along it, and what the plots show as a window on it - drag it to move along the recording, pull an edge to zoom, double-click it for everything; Backspace undoes a move (1.25)
  • A flight log's health check findings, once the view is open, wait beside the timeline as N to look at (they no longer cover a plot; a click opens the list, × puts it away) and each is a ◆ mark on the timeline - a click plots its signals in a new tab (findings close together: one mark, a list)
  • New folder in the dialog (saving: straight into it); on a file or folder Rename (F2) and Delete (Del: asked, then to the recycle bin - Windows, macOS, the freedesktop trash on Linux); only in the user's own folders (home, data drives), never a file open in the app
  • Places beside the folder: the folders of the open files, favourite folders (★ next to the path; drag to reorder), recent folders, home / Desktop / Documents / Downloads and the drives
  • Ctrl+P: quick open of recent files and folders
  • Time axis… (right-click a file): another column as the time (CSV / text, MAT, Parquet), its unit - ready conversions (ms / µs / ns / min / h → s, s → ms / µs / min) or any scale, a separate scale for columns with a time of their own - and the offset; checks before the change (goes up and down, repeats, missing values, gaps, the unit the name says) and what it changes (plots showing the column, new signals and edits computed against time, other open files); the same change on linked files; one Undo. Kept in the session, in refresh and in live mode
  • Columns with a time column of their own (found by name: Speed + Speed_time, msg.roll + msg.time_boot_ms, or alternating time, Speed, time, RPM) are drawn against their own time – CSV / text, MAT, and a .tlog that is a text table (Import options to turn it off)

docs.title: File list
docs.text:
• Every signal with its unit (kept apart from the name, never cut off), its sample rate (wider panel, and the tooltip with the number of samples) and a small picture of the whole signal (spikes included; only the rows on screen fetch theirs)
  • Checkboxes only while signals are selected (Ctrl + click; Shift + click or Shift + drag for a range - each new press of Shift adds another range; select all of a search, or a group's own checkbox / Ctrl+click on the group for all of it): plot them (one undo step), change them (x*8, sin(x), sin(x) + Speed – x is each of them in turn, Speed the one of its own file), or make new signals from them; a right-click on any selected signal offers the same for all of them. After an action the selection stays for the next one, and the next Ctrl / Shift + click starts a new selection; Esc clears it
  • While searching, files and groups of the results can still be closed and opened, or all at once (Collapse all / Expand all)
  • A flight log with more than 40 signals lists its groups closed, except those with signals on the tab's plots (more than 200 signals: all closed); the template suggestions fold away once something is plotted (▸ Templates (3) opens them)

docs.title: Import settings
docs.text: • Settings chosen in Import options are remembered for that folder. Auto-detection still comes first; the remembered settings are used only when auto-detection does not recognise a file (so other files in the folder are never misread). A note says when they were used, with Forget

docs.title: Opening from outside
docs.text: • Open with in Explorer (the installer offers it for .bin, .tlog, .ulg, .mcap, .mat, .csv, .parquet, .h5 and makes .svsession sessions open with the app; your default programs stay as they are) and SignalViewer file… on the command line: when the app is already running the files open in it (its window comes forward) instead of in a second app; several files chosen together end up in one app; --new-window for a separate one

docs.title: Refresh & live
docs.text: • Refresh all files (file panel ⟳, F5 / Ctrl+R): files unchanged on disk are not read again. Each file's row shows when the version on screen was saved to the disk (hover: when it was read); a file saved again since turns amber (↻) - only its date is checked, every few seconds - and a click or F5 reads it; the message after a refresh says per file whether it was read again (and when that version was saved) or not changed on the disk. Live: refreshes every file first, then once a second reads only what was added (CSV rows, .bin / .tlog messages; a MAT, ULog, MCAP, HDF5 or Parquet file is read again once it is quiet for a moment, and at least every 2 s while a program keeps saving it). A green dot marks files that are still being written; the status bar shows "2 of 5 updating". Settings (▾ next to Live): stop after N s without new data (10 s – 15 min, or never; default 1 min), new files in the same folders with the same name pattern (run_013.csv after run_012.csv, 00000043.BIN): ask / open automatically / ignore, follow last N seconds. Files opened during live mode are followed too. A time (cursor) at the end of the recording moves on with the newest data, so the values read at it and the objects on the map and in 3D show the latest state (live mode puts it there when it starts; a time moved back stays, End follows again); an object whose track ends a moment before the newest data holds its last state. Try it without a logger: python tools/live_demo.py writes an aircraft and a ship that keep moving

docs.title: New runs, same work
docs.text:
• Replace the input files… (file panel, command palette) or Open a session with new files… (command palette, or the icon next to a recent session on the welcome screen): the same layout, formulas, edits (ƒ), axes and cursors with new input files
  • For each file the newest file in the same folder with the same name pattern is suggested (run_012 → run_013), or choose any other
  • Before opening, each new file is checked for the signals the work uses (missing ones are listed)
  • Copy the work to another file… (right-click a file): a file already open, or one to open, gets that file's work, each part on its own - its changes (ƒ), the signals made from it (derived of derived too), its signals in the plots (on the same plots to compare, beside each plot in the same tab, in a copy of each tab that uses it, or not at all); the original stays as it is, and it can be repeated for more files. Suggests the open files and the newest file with the same name pattern, checks the target first, and can turn on Link plots and Link operations (each on its own) for what comes next
  • A new signal made from two files belongs to one of them: the sources written with their file ({run_b.csv:Speed}, in an expression of x or a Formula) and a Compare difference's baseline are kept (params.pinned), the others say whose it is - so Copy the work, Link operations and Clear this file handle it like any signal of that file. Signals of two files with no recorded intent are listed in the copy dialog, each made for the new file when ticked
  • Clear this file ▸ (right-click a file): its signals out of every plot, its changes (ƒ) undone, the signals made from it deleted - each on its own or all; the other files keep their work; one Undo
  • Replacing the current files offers Back to the previous files

docs.title: Start over
docs.text:
• Clear ▾ (the Recordings bar; Ctrl+K; the ⋯ above the plots: Clear all plots of this tab, and Back to the previous zoom): this tab's plots
  • The other tabs
  • All tabs (one empty tab)
  • All tabs + notes + derived signals + in-place edits, the files stay open - each undone by the toast's Undo or Ctrl+Z
  • Clear everything (with confirmation): closes all files too — files on disk are never touched

docs.title: ArduPilot logs (.bin)
docs.text:
• DataFlash logs read directly (no pymavlink): about 50 MB/s
  • Very large logs: one pass over the file on several cores without copying it into memory; above 64 MB the values stay in the file until a signal is used (a 16 M-sample signal is read in about 0.3 s) within a memory budget, and fields the log keeps as float32 stay float32 - a 1.2 GB log opens in about 7 s with under 0.5 GB of memory. Its index (time vectors and message positions) is kept in the cache: the same log opens again in a moment (about 0.03 s), only while it is unchanged
  • Every message type keeps its own time (TimeUS), so IMU at 400 Hz and GPS at 5 Hz are not resampled onto each other
  • Sensors with several instances split (IMU[0].AccX, IMU[1].AccX)
  • Units and multipliers from the log's FMTU/UNIT/MULT (GPS[0].Alt [m], cm → m)
  • Flight modes by name (Copter / Plane / Rover / Sub, detected from the log) and EV events by name
  • Text fields (MSG…) as state signals
  • PARM values and MSG texts in the load report
  • Damaged blocks skipped (resync); what the damage made look like data is left out and counted in the note after opening - the message just before a damaged block, and an instance only the damage had (IMU[149] next to IMU[0] / IMU[1])
  • A faulty firmware's message type (1.26) - written with another length than its FMT, an FMT listing more or fewer column names than values, or no FMT at all - is found from the chain of messages, left out by name in the note, and everything else is read; only a log that is mostly damage (under 20 % readable) is refused
  • Live mode reads only the newly written messages. Checked value-by-value against pymavlink. Test log generator: python tools/make_test_bin.py out.bin [--live 30]

docs.title: MAVLink telemetry (.tlog)
docs.text: • What Mission Planner / QGroundControl / MAVProxy record from the radio link. Message definitions from pymavlink (ArduPilot dialect), decoded per message type with numpy (a 3.5 MB log in about 0.4 s; values identical to pymavlink). Units converted (degE7 → deg, mV → V, cm → m, cdeg → deg…), enums by name, flight mode by name (ArduPilot per vehicle type; PX4 main/sub modes), HEARTBEAT.armed; arrays per element, unused battery cells → empty; the ground station's own messages left out, other components / vehicles tagged (ATTITUDE[c154].roll). Messages that carry the autopilot's clock (time_boot_ms, or time_usec when it is boot time) are placed at their own time, not at their receive time - no radio delay in them. Checks: STATUSTEXT with its real severity, mode changes, arm / disarm, PARAM_VALUE. Live mode reads only new packets

docs.title: PX4 logs (.ulg)
docs.text: • Read with pyulog: one signal per topic field (vehicle_attitude.q[0], sensor_gps[1].… when a topic has several instances), each topic with its own time; navigation state and arming by name; topics without time stamps skipped (reported); a damaged log opens with what can be read - samples with a time stamp only damage can make (after the log's end, a lone one far out of step), damaged parameters and messages are left out and counted; Checks: logged messages by level, parameters with changes and defaults

docs.title: ROS 2 / Foxglove (.mcap)
docs.text:
• Every numeric field of every topic becomes a signal (imu/accel.vector.x), each topic on its own time (the recording time, seconds from the first message)
  • ROS 2 messages (CDR, decoded from the definitions stored in the file – no ROS installation needed) and JSON channels
  • A ROS time (header.stamp) becomes one value in seconds, text fields become states with their texts, true / false 1 / 0, short arrays one signal per element
  • Images, point clouds, maps and other bulk topics are not decoded, arrays over 16 values and byte blobs are left out, other encodings (protobuf…) named – all listed when the file opens
  • A recording cut off by a crash opens with everything before the cut

docs.title: Parquet (.parquet / .pq)
docs.text:
• Every numeric and true / false column; text and categorical columns become states
  • The time: the column you choose, else the pandas index (date-times in seconds from the start), else a column named like a time, else the first date-time column; no time: sample numbers
  • Columns of other types (lists, structs) are listed as left out

docs.title: HDF5 (.h5 / .hdf5)
docs.text:
• Every numeric dataset (sensors/imu/ax), each column of a matrix up to 16 columns (pos[0]…), each numeric field of a table (pandas / PyTables / records)
  • A group's own time / t / timestamp for its signals, else the file's main time; signals with no time of their length are listed, a file with no time uses sample numbers
  • Damaged parts are skipped and counted, the rest opens

docs.title: CAN
docs.text: • Candump .log, Vector .asc and CAN .csv (time, id, data) decoded with the .dbc files next to the log or in the readers folder: Intel / Motorola, signed, scale / offset, value names, float, multiplexed, 29-bit ids, CAN FD payloads; unknown ids counted - our own decoder (MIT)

docs.title: Your own formats
docs.text:
• A Python file in the readers folder (~/.signalviewer/readers) with @reader(extensions=[".kv"]) returning the time and the signals: those files open like the built-in types (file dialog, drag & drop, Python, command line); re-read when saved; errors name the line; in the app a reader runs in a process of its own - one that crashes Python or never ends (SV_READER_TIMEOUT, default 600 s) is stopped and the app keeps working
  • Binary layouts (ICD): a *.icd.json there describes packets (sync, id, length, header time; fields with type, byte order, scale / offset, unit, bits, value names) and raw recordings open as <packet>.<field> [unit] - see Command line and formats

docs.title: Text values
docs.text: • A CSV column of text (IDLE / ARMED / FLYING…) becomes a state signal with its texts (up to 1000 different; more → skipped, e.g. IDs). Shown as text everywhere: cursor, legend, hover, value axis. Live mode adds new texts as they appear. Sparse columns (blank cells) keep the last value. The cursor shows the value in force for states (never an interpolation)

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
• Tabs (rename, duplicate, close, close others, drag to reorder; many tabs: an All tabs list next to +, the active tab always in view, the mouse wheel scrolls them, Ctrl+PageUp / PageDown, Go to tab in the command palette)
  • Any layout up to 9 plots (one layout button: the common ones, a grid picker or type rows × columns; drop a signal on a plot's right or bottom edge to split it)
  • Shrinking the layout removes the extra plots (Undo)
  • Drag the gaps between plots to resize
  • Time / X-Y / FFT / Map per plot (longitude + latitude signals; wheel = zoom, drag = pan, double-click = fit; the Map background picker - online maps ☁, My maps, or the offline map that ships with the app – terrain shading and colour by height, water, rivers, roads and runways, place and airport names in Hebrew or English; detailed for Israel and its surroundings (elevation ~130 m, roads down to regional roads, villages), the rest of the world coarser; it also fills in for online tiles that cannot be had without internet)
  • Objects on the map: an aircraft, UAV, drone, missile, ship or vehicle whose latitude / longitude (and altitude, heading, pitch, roll) come from signals – from any open files, filled in from their names (GPS.Lat / Lng / Alt, ATT.Yaw…; MAVLink 1e7 degrees handled) – chosen by typing their names, each with the unit it is in and ƒ to change it on the spot (radians → degrees…) – drawn as an icon at the timeline's time, pointing along its heading or, without one, where it moves; its track follows the timeline's mode; Track colour: the object's own, by a state (the flight mode by itself, in the mode lane's colours) or by a value (a colour scale), with a key in the map's corner (3D too) - the plain track of the same position takes the object's colour; follow keeps it in the middle; edit / remove from its chip (Undo)
  • 3D view (a plot mode): the earth with the bundled terrain and the same map tiles, the plot's objects as 3D models (aircraft, UAV, drone, missile, ship, vehicle) at the timeline's time with heading, pitch and roll, their tracks, names, and a readout (altitude, height above ground, attitude); altitude given above sea level, above the take-off point or above the ground; a bar to choose the object (its values in a data box that can be hidden: position, altitude, height above ground, heading, pitch, roll, ground speed, climb), the camera – general, or on the object (turning goes around it, zooming goes towards it) – and a second / third object: a dashed line to each with the distance, and in the box the horizontal distance, height difference, slant range and bearing (on the WGS84 ellipsoid); works with no internet (CesiumJS ships with the app, no Cesium ion); on a computer without graphics acceleration it switches to lighter settings and says so
  • Own time: a 3D plot can leave the timeline and get its own bar, play and speed (the other plots keep the timeline's; framed so it shows), and go back
  • Events: the log's errors, warnings and mode changes as marks on the tracks
  • Measure: two clicks on the ground give the distance over the ground, straight and the height difference
  • Image: the view as a PNG, at the screen's size or at twice it (for a report)
  • Manual axis limits
  • Link X and link Y (the plots of a column line up: the same moment is at the same place in each, whatever their units; an Envelope plot zooms with them)
  • Drag-zoom, wheel-zoom, pan (Alt+drag or middle button), zoom history (Backspace)
  • Min/max decimation that follows the zoom down to raw samples
  • Clear plot / clear all (Undo)

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
• Virtualized list (thousands of signals)
  • Grouping by name prefix; a big group (12 or more) nests again by the rest of the name (IMU[0] ▸ Acc ▸ …)
  • My groups: select signals ▸ right-click ▸ Group these / Add to a group ▸ New group…, named as you like; / nests (Nav/IMU inside Nav). Above the files; drag signals onto a group; rename, take a signal out, remove the group (the signals stay), add the whole group to a plot. Any open file's signals and made signals; saved with the session; Ctrl+Z
  • A made signal (Create signals): Rename… (the plots, the groups and the signals made from it follow), Change the formula… and Delete (also the Delete key, also several) - what was made from it is asked about and deleted too; one Undo puts all of it back in every plot
  • Smart search: substrings, letters in order (“spd” → Speed), one typo (“sepeed” → Speed); exact matches win
  • Right-click: add, new plot, use as X, Create signal ▸ (derivative, integral, other operations… – Create signals opens with the signal chosen)

docs.title: Legend names
docs.text:
• One data file → signal name only
  • Several files → each file has a colour and a short tag (A, B… – rename it in File options, click it in the file list to change the colour): the legend, cursor values, statistics and signal pickers show the tag; the tooltip has the full name and path; the same signal from several files in one plot is coloured by file (Colour by file in the plot menu for all)
  • Exports and reports name the file (“signal · file”), with as many parent folders as needed (“A/test.csv”, “x/A/test.csv”)

docs.title: Legend place
docs.text:
• Statistics of the shown window (1.27; a plot's menu ▸ Legend): the lowest, mean and highest value of each line over the time on screen, beside it in the legend, recomputed with every pan and zoom - fast on signals of tens of millions of samples. The mean is the plain mean of the samples in the window, not weighted by time.
  • A plot's menu ▸ Legend: Automatic (above while it fits in two rows, else a column beside the plot), Above the plot, Beside the plot, Hidden (a button says how many signals and shows it again)
  • Beside the plot: a row per signal, the values in one aligned column, a filter above 8 signals, the width dragged (double-click: as it was)
  • The values never move the legend: each keeps a place as wide as the widest it had, and the header does not get lower while the pointer is in the plot; the time under the pointer is in the plot's corner; a name that says its unit (Roll [deg]) does not repeat it after the value
  • The pointer on an entry (above or beside) draws its line in front, the plot's others faint
  • 20 colours for new lines

docs.title: Legend chips
docs.text:
• Click: properties
  • Ctrl+click: select several and edit them together (scale, offset, time offset, width, display, remove), change the signals themselves or make new signals from all of them (also on the right-click of a selected chip)
  • Drag to reorder or to another plot (Ctrl: copy)
  • Right-click: properties, states, states only (hide the line, keep the markers), move up/down, copy to new plot, use as X, Create signal ▸, remove
  • Right-click: To the right axis – a second value axis with its own scale and unit for a signal in other units (offered when you add one); reports and images draw both axes
  • A setpoint beside its measured value (DesRoll / Roll, RATE.RDes / RATE.R, roll_sp / roll, <topic>_setpoint.x / <topic>.x; the words des, desired, dem, demand, cmd, command, commanded, sp, setpoint, set, target, tgt, ref, reference - before or after the name, with a separator or in camel case) is drawn dashed and a little faded, its swatch dashed; Inspector ▸ Line: Auto / Solid / Dashed (a choice by hand wins)
  • Plot the commanded / measured pairs (a file's menu in the signal list, for that file; Ctrl+K, for every open file): a new tab with a plot per pair - the measured value and its setpoint dashed - in one step (one Undo); a report of that tab holds them
  • Line styles (since 1.24): solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot (Inspector ▸ Line; in reports and saved pictures too); Settings ▸ New lines sets the width and style of every new line, Apply to all open plots gives them to the lines drawn (one Undo); Style the lines… in a group's menu (signal list) or Style these lines… for the legend selection: one colour or the palette, a width and a style for that group's lines in this plot, this tab or every tab (one Undo)
  • Plots change places (since 1.24): drag a plot by its ⠿ onto another, Move to… in its menu, or Ctrl+Shift+arrows; the cells keep their sizes
  • A plot goes to another tab or into another plot (since 1.25): Move to… lists the other tabs and New tab, or drop the plot on a tab's name (Ctrl: a copy) - it arrives as it is (lines, axes, cursors, a map's objects and pair); Add its lines to… (Shift+drop on a plot) joins a plot's lines to another of the same kind. One Undo each; a full tab refuses and says why
  • One plot at a time (since 1.25): M or the layout button - the active plot fills the tab, 1 - 9 show the others, Esc returns; the layout is not changed
  • A line that would look flat beside larger ones is offered To the right axis or To its own plot (since 1.25) - from the values, so files with no units are covered; nothing moves by itself
  • The ⋯ button of a plot is always in the head's far corner (since 1.25), whatever the head holds

docs.title: Plot menus
docs.text: • The plot's type is one button with its name (Time ▾: Time, X-Y, XYZ, Map, 3D, FFT, Step response, Spectrogram, Envelope, Video); right-click in a plot: cursor here, second cursor here, note here, previous zoom, show everything, export data, save / copy image, axis limits, clear plot (the ⋯ button has the plot's part)

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text: • One top row, the same in every work area: the areas as one switch (Recordings · Sweeps), then the Recordings tools (no File menu, F35): open / save session, Templates ▾ (save a template, a new collection), Live ▾ (it follows the open files and MAVLink, so it is the Recordings area's), undo / redo, Clear ▾ (what to clear, see Start over) and the Inspector; Ctrl+K, Settings, day / night (one click), language and the Help menu. The plot tabs, with + (a new tab) and ▾ (the views menu: a new tab, a template or collection, the tabs a template left out), are in the stage bar above the plots (1.27: the plots gained 40 pixels of height) - opening files is in the file list (Ctrl+O), recent files Ctrl+P; Settings (theme, text size, time as seconds or a clock; kept between starts, not changed by sessions; the disk space the app uses for speed - CSV cache and log indexes, copies of files dropped into a browser, map tiles - each with its size and Clear; and the results kept in memory to be fast - changed and derived signals, spectra, plot summaries, statistics - with its limit, SV_MEMCACHE_MB, default 1024) and Help menu (keyboard shortcuts, the examples, copy error details, about)

docs.title: Zoom
docs.text:
• A drag zooms by its direction: nearly sideways = time, nearly up or down = values, diagonal = a box (no mode to set); for one drag Shift = values, Ctrl = always a box. The wheel zooms time (over the value axis, or with Shift: values)
  • Wheel over the value axis zooms values only, over the time axis time only; Shift+wheel values only, Ctrl+wheel both, Alt+wheel time only
  • Alt+drag pans (follows the mode)
  • The wheel follows the size of the scroll (a trackpad zooms smoothly; a sideways swipe moves along the time) and one gesture is one step back
  • Backspace undoes one zoom step of both axes
  • R / double-click reset both

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
• A bar under the plots for the whole recording (all open files, time offsets included); its handle is the cursor – drag or click it, arrows move 1 %, Home / End jump to the start / end
  • A row per file showing when it has data, log errors / warnings and your notes as marks to jump to
  • Play / pause (P) at × real time (×0.25 … ×60), a zoomed time plot follows the time
  • The plots show all + cursor, up to the time (they draw themselves) or the last N seconds – time plots, X-Y plots (by each point's time), maps (the whole track faint, the part shown in full colour) and spectrograms
  • Can be made small (a thin bar that still drags)
  • Time written in seconds as recorded (the axes' number) or, in Settings, a clock from the start
  • Saved in sessions

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
• A plot in Video mode plays a local video (mp4, webm, mov…) with the timeline: moving the cursor moves the video, play plays both, and playing or seeking in the video moves the cursor
  • Line up… then Lock here: put the video and the cursor on the same moment (take-off, a step) and they stay together (the offset can also be typed)
  • Saved with the session, part of Undo
  • "No video at this time" outside the clip

docs.title: State display
docs.text: • A state lane per signal: a coloured block per state with its text inside (same state = same colour everywhere). Lanes alone fill the plot one under the other with their names; next to lines they sit along the bottom and the value axis makes room. Stretches with too many changes to draw are hatched (zoom in). Text signals start as lanes; Line shows them as steps with the texts on the value axis

docs.title: Shared state lanes
docs.text:
• The flight mode once per tab: when a tab's time plots share the time axis (X linked, one column, two or more), its shared lanes - the flight mode of the ArduPilot views - are not drawn in every plot (they get the height back) but once: in the overview strip above the plots when it shows that signal (its default row), else in a band right above the plots, lined up with their time axis and following the zoom. Cursors 1 / 2 and the pointer over a plot are lines on that row, and the state under each is outlined and named (1 · AUTO); in the band a click on a stretch puts the cursors on its edges, Shift+click zooms to it. A plot's ⋯ ▸ State lanes in this plot too shows them in that plot again.
  • Conditions (rail ▸ Investigate): named, kept in the session; written with signal names like a formula plus and / or / not and state texts (Mode == "AUTO"), looked for in every open file that has the signals (a file without them says which are missing); options: an exit condition (hysteresis), leave out stretches shorter than, join stretches closer than. The editor counts the stretches while you type (the change when editing: "6 → 4"), and when it never holds says the range of what it reads. Each condition: shown / hidden, its colour, its count (per file on hover), ⋯ edit, duplicate, And with / Or with another (combined, following its parts), delete (one undo; conditions combined from it go with it). Click the name or press ] / [: the next / previous stretch, both cursors on it, the condition in focus. On the time plots: the condition in focus shaded over the whole height, the other shown ones thin strips along the top
  • The stretches of the condition in focus (Investigate panel): a table - file, start, length and the max / min / mean of a signal the condition reads, per stretch; sort by any column, a click zooms there with both cursors on it, Copy table. Together in a new tab: an "occurrences" plot - every stretch of the signal on top of each other, lined up at their start, end or peak (the dashed line), with the share of the longest stretch before and after, one colour per file, thin stretches and their mean bold (the first 200). What differs inside: every numeric signal of the files, ranked by how far its mean inside the stretches is from outside, in times its usual spread outside (↑ / ↓, outside → inside); a click opens it in a plot of its own (in every file it is in), Ctrl+click adds it to the active plot
  • What changed first (What changed? on the selection bar): by default every signal of the event's file (the file whose signal is most unusual in the span - also signals on no plot), or the signals of the tab, or every signal of their files - each one's usual level and noise read well before the span (a signal already drifting steadily there - a straight line explains it much better than a level, a curve does not - is judged against that drift carried on) (max(span, 2 s), ending max(span, 1 s) before it, said in the panel), its first move beyond 4 times that noise for 3 samples in a row from there to the end of the span (a state: a new value) - a ranked list of candidates with a small picture each, ↑ / ↓ and how many times the noise, the time from the span's start and the sample rate; rows the rates cannot order are grouped "together" (measured from the group's first row), a group with its time range, closed / taken out at once, long groups 5 at a time; under each row, the same signal in the other open files at the same time (↑ 18× · −0.2 s, or no change); a filter by name; a row or group taken out (×) leaves the list and its dashed line the plots, bring them back; "N did not change" and "no data" apart; a warning that earlier is not proof of cause (and the resolution when rates differ); dashed lines on the time plots at each moment (gone with the panel). Tick rows: in a new tab (stacked, linked), Lag between the two picked - normalised cross-correlation on one grid: "B follows A by 120 ms (match 0.9)", or no clear relation, the opposite way, or not one number (a repeating signal); its curve; Show aligned shifts B on the active plot (undo). A click on a name opens it in a plot of its own; Ctrl+click adds it to the active plot
  • Runs × conditions (Investigate panel, under the conditions): a row per open run - its parameters (signals that hold one value the whole run, numbers in the file name such as mass2.4, wind=8, run_012; only those that differ between runs) - and a column per condition: how many stretches, or how long in all; sort by any column; a cell far from the rest of its column is marked (beyond 3 robust spreads, or the odd one out when the rest agree); a click opens that run at the condition's first stretch; Copy table; two columns against each other (a point per run, a fitted line, r). Open a folder of runs… opens every CSV / MAT / Parquet / HDF5 file of a folder (up to 200) - a Monte-Carlo set or a sweep
  • The strip's rows: by default the run's phase signal; + adds a state signal (texts, or a few whole numbers) or a named condition as a row, a row's name opens Replace with…, Move up / down, Remove (kept in the session; a condition deleted takes its row). Picking moments on the strip (a row's stretches in the same colours as its lane on the plots): a click picks a stretch and every stretch with the same value; Ctrl / Shift+click adds - in the same row as "or", in another row as "and" - a Selection row shows the result (shaded on the run's plots too), its count, and Save as a condition (state rows as Name == "TEXT", plain conditions inlined, others combined); Esc clears; a double-click zooms to a stretch
  • The run at a glance (a strip above the plots, on by default, × hides it - remembered; its time axis lined up under the first time plot's): the run of the active plot (a choice with several files), its length, its rows (above), where the plots are zoomed, and automatic flags - a signal that moves sample to sample holding one exact value for max(2 s, 5% of the run) (frozen?), flat at its own maximum or minimum for ≥ 0.3 s while rarely there (out of headroom?), no samples for 20 times the usual step (and ≥ 0.5 s), a sample or two far from both neighbours and back (glitch?); never in the first or last 5% of the run (ground, idle); at most 30, close ones as one marker with their list; a click puts both cursors on it. Places worth a look, not faults
  • Findings: a note's status in the Inspector - mark (as before), open, explained, fault, rejected hypothesis; the first time it becomes a finding it keeps the view it was found in (the tab, its zoom, the cursors) and ⌖ brings it back. Steps so far (Investigate panel): conditions saved (with their count), what changed first, lags, what differs, overlays, errors per axis, finding statuses - recorded as you work, each with its view, ticked for the report; grouped by kind, a group ticked / closed / removed at once, All in the report / None, a filter when there are more than 5, "4 of 6 in the report". The report's investigation (Report panel, Include the investigation, on when there is any): Findings (a table, open first), each with its plot at its view in a "Findings" tab of the report; hypotheses checked and rejected; the ticked analysis steps; the conditions per run; how to reproduce (the files and how they were read - time column, unit, offset - the conditions, the new signals' formulas, the edits, the version) - in HTML, PDF and Word. Range notes now keep their end time in reports
  • The selection bar: with both cursors on, a small bar above the span in the active plot - Note, Find similar (a condition on the signal most unusual inside the span, of all the tab's time plots - its 90th-percentile distance from its usual level, read as for What changed first - half way from that level to there, opened in the editor; without an answer, the plot's first line), What changed?
  • Templates keep the conditions: a template saved from the workspace takes its conditions along (written by signal name); opening it adds the ones not there yet (by name; combined ones stay combined), counted on the open files at once; the library shows "N conditions" on it
  • One into each plot (▾ beside Plot them, or right-click a selection or a group): several signals, one into each time plot of the tab that has a line - paired by the part of the names that differs within each side (TruePos_X / _Y / _Z ↔ NavPos_X / _Y / _Z, [0] / [1] / [2], Roll / Pitch / Yaw; picked in any order), else by order from the active plot; more signals than plots: new plots for the rest. The set added has one colour in every plot (the palette colour furthest in hue from the lines there); a message lists the pairs and undoes them (one step). Each in a new plot is in the same menu
  • The error per axis (⋯ on a plot with two lines): Error: B − A for that plot, Error in every plot with two lines (n): each error a new signal (second line − first, made once and reused), all in a new tab "Errors", a plot per axis titled RMS · mean · max |e| at its time - over the time both have data, B on A's samples - and worst in AUTO (…) when one flight mode (the file's phase signal) has 1.5 × the RMS of the next; the cursor on the largest error of all; the step recorded
  • Where a lane is shown, from one menu (right-click the lane itself, its chip, or the signal in the list): this plot only, every plot of this tab, or every time plot, all tabs (new tabs too) - one place at a time - and Remove this lane. The built-in views put the flight mode on every plot of the tab; templates keep tab lanes (not the all-tabs ones)
  • Always as a state (every plot, every file): by the signal's name - every plot showing it becomes a lane at once, and so does every later add, in any open file; switched off, they become lines. Signals with texts are lanes unless switched off
  • A lane's name sits in the margin left of it, never over the data; hovering a lane shows the state there, its stretch and where the lane is shown. Several lanes under lines share at most a quarter of the plot (thinner lanes, no text when too thin)

docs.title: States
docs.text: • Click a block of a state lane → both cursors on that stretch (statistics cover exactly it); Shift+click → zoom to it. Statistics only while a state has a value ("while MODE = LOITER": time in that state, number of stretches)

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
• Space on/off
  • Click / drag
  • Two cursors with ΔT, Δ and Δ/ΔT
  • With two cursors each line's chip in the legend shows its change between them (Δ, cursor 2 − cursor 1, in its unit) beside its value (1.25)
  • Values at full resolution
  • Values drawn on the plot (optional)

docs.title: Values under the pointer
docs.text:
• Hover over a plot (no cursor needed): the legend shows each signal's value under the pointer, from the points already drawn (no server round-trip)
  • Units taken from names such as Speed [km/h] or Temp (°C) are shown with values and on the value axis (imu[1] is not a unit)
  • Unit conversions in Change this signal…: rad ↔ deg, rad/s ↔ deg/s, m/s ↔ km/h ↔ kn ↔ mph ↔ ft/min, m ↔ ft ↔ km ↔ NM, m/s² ↔ g, °C ↔ °F ↔ K, Pa ↔ hPa ↔ psi, ms / µs → s, deg·1e7 → deg - the ones from the signal's unit first; an in-place change (stacked, Undo, sessions), and the unit shown on the axis, in the file list and the legend becomes the new one (or one you type)

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text:
• Cursor values (active plot / all)
  • Statistics for the visible range or between cursors (on uneven sampling – a variable-step solver, a changing logging rate – mean, RMS and std are weighted by time, marked ⏱; dropouts are not given the samples around them), copy as a table
  • Signal properties incl. time offset per signal

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • N (or + in the Inspector) notes the moment at the cursor - with two cursors, the time between them (a shaded span); notes show on every time plot, are listed in the Inspector (go to / edit / remove), saved with the session, undoable, and listed in reports (with markers on the PDF / Word plots)

docs.title: Formulas
docs.text:
• Write a new signal as an equation, e.g. 2*Speed - RPM/95 + where(Gear > 2, 1, 0)
  • Signal names as they are, {file.csv:Speed} when a name is in several files
  • Autocomplete while typing (Tab / Enter)
  • + - * / ^ %, comparisons (1 / 0), abs sqrt exp log log10 sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sign floor ceil round min max clip where deriv integ smooth smooth_s lowpass highpass (lowpass(Speed, 5): −3 dB cut-off in Hz, filtered in time - never across a gap, the same after a change of logging rate; smooth_s(Speed, 0.5): a centred average over 0.5 s; smooth(x, n): over n samples), t, pi, e
  • Signals from different files are aligned in time
  • A state signal (a flight mode, a gear, a text column, a few whole numbers) is read as the value in force at each moment - never interpolated between two modes (the same in conditions: Mode == 5 starts when the mode was entered); which numeric signals are states is detected (a few whole-number levels) and can be corrected by name in the signal list: right-click ▸ Read between samples as ▸ Automatic (what was detected) / A state (held) / A value (interpolated) - saved with the session, undoable, followed by the cursor values, formulas, conditions and operations; a derived signal saved with "hold": false keeps the old alignment - derived signals in a session saved before 1.23 are restored so, their numbers unchanged
  • Clear errors (“Unknown signal: Spede. Did you mean Speed?”)
  • Evaluated safely on the server (a closed list of operations, no code execution)
  • Saved as a formula, updates when sources change

docs.title: Formula help
docs.text: • While typing a formula (Analysis → Formula, and Change this signal… on a signal's right-click): suggestions for functions with what each one does, variables (x = the signal, t = time, pi, e) and signals; a function goes in with its parentheses and the caret inside; the arguments of the function the caret is in are shown with the current one highlighted (smooth(x, n=10)); Ctrl+Space lists everything. Checked while typing: unclosed brackets, unknown names with did you mean…?; in an expression of x (Change this signal…, Expression in x), other signals of the same file by name - sin(x) + Speed - or of one particular file - {run_b.csv:Speed} - suggested while typing; a name some chosen file lacks is named with those files, and a name with spaces typed without braces is answered with the braced one

docs.title: param() in formulas
docs.text: • x / param("BATT_CAPACITY") - a parameter's value from the open flight log, with suggestions of the names and their values; param("flight.bin:NAME") when several logs differ

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
• A derivative or integral of a signal's real updates: at its own, slower rate (Hz), or where another signal (a 0 / 1 flag) is 1 - a value computed slower than it is logged no longer gives zero, then a spike; in formulas deriv(x, 10), deriv(x, {Flag})
  • One signal (derivative, integral, abs, negate, normalize, k·x + c, smoothing and RMS over a window in seconds (never across a gap), low/high-pass (in time: each stretch between gaps on its own, an uneven stretch on an even grid of its usual step) – 4th-order Butterworth, run both ways so nothing is delayed, with the cut-off at the −3 dB point of the result (the filter is designed for the two passes); a cut-off it cannot use is explained, never the raw signal under the filter's name; your own expression in x – x*8, sin(x), sin(x) + Speed with another signal of the same file – on one signal or on each of several), two signals, several signals
  • Apply to the selected signals or to the whole plot
  • Preview (dashed) before creating
  • Derived signals keep their formula and update when sources change
  • Missing values stay missing (since 1.23): a sum, mean, min, max or norm of several signals is missing where one of them is; an integral is unknown from a gap on (never counted as 0); in a formula a comparison, not or where with a missing value is missing (and / or only when the other side does not decide), and a value that is infinite (1/0) becomes missing and is counted. In Create signals the sum, mean, min, max, norm and the integral have Missing values: Keep missing (the default) or Use the signals that have a value / Bridge the gap (saved as "nan": "skip") - such a signal is marked in the list of derived signals (skipped missing, gaps bridged; hover: how many samples, which gaps); an integral that became unknown after a gap, or a formula with infinite values, is marked too. Derived signals in sessions saved before 1.23 keep the numbers they had (restored as "nan": "legacy")
  • Two signals, A − B: how far apart they are - RMS, mean and largest |A − B| over the time both have and per stretch of a state (each flight mode), the worst stretch marked (a simulation against the flight, a model against the test)

docs.title: Spectra
docs.text:
• FFT or Welch, window, log scale
  • Signals with gaps or lost samples are put on an even time grid first (the frequencies stay right; the plot shows how many gaps were bridged)
  • Motor orders: pick an RPM / ESC signal and the spectrum is marked at 1×, 2×, 3× its mean rotation rate over the same window, plus the blade-pass frequency for 2–5 blades

docs.title: Spectrogram
docs.text: • Plot mode next to FFT: frequency over time of the plot's first signal, over the tab's time window (zoom, link, cursor as usual); window length and highest frequency selectable; time / frequency / dB on hover; in reports too

docs.title: Coordinate frames
docs.text:
• Create signals ▸ Several ▸ Smooth a vector: the 2-3 components of one vector (position, velocity) each a centred moving average over a window in seconds (the same at any rate), never across a gap (a step over 10x the usual one), latitude / longitude unwrapped across ±180; one new signal per component, as one group. Angles are not smoothed
  • Map / 3D objects: Position from latitude / longitude, ECEF, NED or ENU (NED / ENU with a reference point: the first sample of other signals or typed numbers), and Smooth position (s) - made as derived signals when saved, read back when the object is edited (saved unchanged: nothing new is made)
  • Create signals ▸ Frames: NED, ENU, body, ECEF, LLA – a vector (rotated; body needs the attitude as Euler angles or a quaternion) or a position (also moves the origin; NED / ENU from a reference point: the first sample, other signals or numbers)
  • Suggested from the names (GPS position → NED, a NED velocity → body, an IMU acceleration → NED with the log's attitude)
  • The three axes are created as one group (ned_Pos_lla.N/E/D), previewed in the active plot or a plot per axis, and go to the active plot, a new plot each, or none
  • A plain XYZ plot (any three signals, no earth) can be placed on the map

docs.title: Python operations
docs.text:
• Create signals ▸ Python: your own operations as Python files in your operations folder (~/.signalviewer/operations, or one you choose): every function marked @operation(name=…, inputs=…, params={…}) is listed with its description and parameters; it gets the time and the signal(s) as numpy arrays (several inputs aligned onto the first one's time) and returns the new values, or new times and values
  • Make an example writes a file with three operations to start from; Reload after editing; files that do not load are listed with the line
  • The result is a derived signal like any other (preview, live updates, sessions, Undo)
  • Runs in a process of its own: an error names the line in your file, an endless loop is stopped after 2 minutes, a crash does not take the app down
  • Only your folder runs: a session or template keeps just the operation's name

docs.title: Send data from Python
docs.text:
• From Jupyter, a simulation or any script: from signalviewer_push import show; show(t, {"altitude": alt}, name="sim 3") (also show(t, y) and show(dataframe) – index = time)
  • The client is one file, numpy only (Create signals ▸ Python ▸ Save the Python client…)
  • A new name goes into the active plot; the same name again updates it in place (plots, cursor values and signals made from it follow) – send every few simulation steps to watch it run
  • Binary (.npz, data only), to 127.0.0.1 only, with a token the app writes at every start to ~/.signalviewer/push.json (readable by you only)
  • F5 and live mode leave such data alone (there is no file behind it)

docs.title: Choosing many signals
docs.text: • In Analysis, “each of several” and “several signals” use a picker: type part of a name and select all N matching, or tick one by one — the signals do not need to be in a plot. Shortcuts: from the active plot, from the legend selection. Bulk selection uses exact matches only; approximate names are offered one by one

docs.title: Similarity list
docs.text:
• Choose two or more files in Compare: every shared signal is listed at once, ranked by similarity (least similar first, one click to reverse)
  • Match % = 100 − error %, error % = RMS of the difference relative to the baseline's range
  • Colour bar (same ≥ 99 % / close 90–99 % / different < 90 %) and filter pills with counts
  • A small curve shows where in time the difference is (flat = uniform)
  • Click a row: the signal from every file in the active plot, with the details below (Shift+click: new plot)
  • Computed in the background with quiet progress; changing the choice cancels the running computation on the server, waits 0.35 s for further changes, and earlier choices are cached
  • The first chosen file is the baseline by default (against the mean, two files would each show half their real difference)
  • Angles (yaw, heading, course… in deg / rad) are compared around the circle: 359° and 1° are 2° apart
  • Pass / fail and the largest difference are judged on every sample of both runs (a short excursion, or one between two samples of a slower golden run, fails) - the same verdict as signalviewer-cli compare

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
• Signals match across files by name, with or without their unit (a simulation's ATT.Roll is the flight log's ATT.Roll [deg]) - also in Align and on the command line (a worked example)
  • The table colours the RMS Δ and correlation cells by how bad they are, for quick scanning
  • Any number of files
  • Baseline run or mean
  • One signal: RMS / max / mean Δ, correlation, tolerance, automatic time alignment (Undo), plot runs / differences
  • Events, one list (Checks ▸ Events): the log's modes, events, errors and messages, the health findings, the conditions' stretches and the plotted signals' limit violations, in time order, each kind a chip; ] / [ jump to the next / previous event of any kind (not plain messages) - the status bar names it (◆ 3/24 · Mode · ALT_HOLD); a focused condition keeps ] / [ for its stretches; Next event / Previous event in the command palette
  • Data quality when a file opens (in the background): per signal - missing values, gaps (the spectra's rule), repeated or backwards time stamps, rate changes (a block median of the step, so jitter and one gap are not changes); states and events are only checked for missing values. A note when there is something to say (Show), a ! badge on the file and a mark on its signals (hover: what); Data quality… in the file's menu lists every signal (click: plot it)
  • Trust badges: a derived signal that rests on an assumption is marked - ≈ on its legend chip, a word in Create signals' list (interpolated: another signal's values read between its samples, linear or nearest; filtered by stretch: a filter run on each stretch between gaps, or on an even grid for uneven samples; skipped missing, gaps bridged, gap: unknown after, infinite → missing), the tooltip saying exactly what; a map / 3D object with an Automatic angle unit shows ≈ with the guess and why; the status bar shows ● Online map while an online map layer is on screen and Network off when the app may not use the network
  • Judge a run (golden run → verdict → report): Compare against starts on a golden run, else a file named as the reference (golden, reference, baseline, nominal, expected), else the first file. Tick ★ Golden run to remember the baseline file with its tolerances; a recording opened later that has at least half of its signals gets Judge it against on the start card - one click opens the golden run beside it, its tolerances and Compare. The verdict opens the panel: per file ✓ all N signals within / ✗ k of N outside; Show the worst failure picks the signal with the largest share outside (its difference over time below); Report… makes a tab of the failing signals (each with every file) and a report with the verdict table first (per signal: the tolerance, each file's ✓ / ✗, share outside and largest difference) - in HTML, PDF and Word
  • Tolerances per signal (the file signalviewer-cli compare --tolerances reads): Tolerance and alignment sets every signal's (± in the signal's unit, %, a time tolerance, the share of samples allowed outside); under the selected signal, its own (empty fields show every signal's, greyed) or Leave out of pass / fail. Signals with their own tolerance are marked ± in the list. Save tolerances… / Open tolerances… write and read that JSON file, so the app and CI judge with the same limits and give the same verdict
  • Comparison table: every signal name found in at least two of the chosen files, with Δ mean and Δ std between files, worst RMS / max Δ, lowest correlation, pass/fail; sort, search, expand a row for each file's mean / std / min / max and its differences from the baseline, plot a row, export everything to CSV
  • Where and why a signal fails (as the Simulink Data Inspector): with a tolerance every signal in the list has ✓ or ✗; the selected signal shows each run's difference from the baseline over time under its numbers, the tolerance band shaded, the stretches outside it in red and listed (a click: both cursors on it and zoom; a click on the chart: the cursor)

docs.title: Compare views
docs.text: • With an autopilot log and a telemetry log of the same flight open: Autopilot log vs telemetry views (roll / pitch in degrees from both, altitude, battery, satellites, ground speed, radio link) with both flight modes on every plot - choose which two files when more are open. Align their time first (it is offered automatically)

docs.title: Same segment across runs
docs.text: • Compare runs ▸ Compare over: A segment: a state signal (flight mode, gear, any text column), a value and which occurrence (1st, 2nd… or last); each file is compared from the start of its own segment, the list shows where it is in each file; clicking a signal opens the files over that segment, lined up at 0, in a tab named after it; the comparison table names it too

docs.title: Align any two files
docs.text: • Right-click a file → Align time with another file works for every file type (CSV, MAT, logs): automatically by signals with the same name in both files (normalised correlation of the overlapping part, judged together with how much overlaps, so a short accidental match does not win); by two signals you pick (any names, any units), optionally only within ±N s of the current alignment (periodic signals); by a moment in a signal of each file - rises / falls through a level (a share of each signal's own range, so units do not matter), the biggest jump, the first change of value, the highest / lowest point, the start of the recording, first / second / third / last occurrence; by the cursors - cursor 1 on a moment in the reference, cursor 2 on the same moment in this file, then right-click the file → Shift this file so T2 falls on T1. Undo

docs.title: Align two recordings
docs.text: • An autopilot log (.bin / .ulg) and a telemetry log (.tlog) of the same flight: noticed automatically ("looks like the same flight – Align"), or right-click a file → Align time with another file. Three independent methods, shown with how reliable they are and whether they agree: autopilot boot clock (the .tlog carries it - exact for every message that has it), matching events (the same texts, mode changes, arm / disarm), signal correlation (ATT.Roll ~ ATTITUDE.roll… or two signals you pick; units do not matter). Apply & check opens a tab with the same quantity and both flight modes on top of each other. Undo. Test pair: python tools/make_same_flight.py out_dir

docs.title: Checks and the file
docs.text: For any recording, not only flight logs (1.27: the Log panel became Checks).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• One verdict, then tinted cards (green / yellow / red edge): your limits, the data quality (gaps, repeated or backwards time, missing values) and, for a log, its health check; a card's signals plot with one click
  • The run at a glance shows a Checks: n failed · m to look at chip that opens Checks on that run

docs.title: The file
docs.text: • The structure of any recording: a log's message types, a ROS bag's topics, a MATLAB file's structs, a table's column groups - each with its rate, samples, units and gaps, the time base and the values at the cursor; a live link's file as it grows; a click on a column plots it

docs.title: Parameters of a run
docs.text:
• One list for every format: a flight log's parameters, a MATLAB file's scalars, texts and struct fields, signals that hold one value the whole run, numbers in the file name - each with where it came from
  • Compare with another open file: only what differs (a parameter changed during a flight counts by its start and its end); Runs × conditions in Compare shows a MATLAB file's settings and a log's parameters when they differ between the runs

docs.title: At a glance and profiles
docs.text:
• The run at a glance: up to four numbers per run (the maximum, minimum, mean, first or last value of a signal over the whole run) in mono beside its name - a click goes to its time, ⋯ unpins it, a signal the file does not have is said, not hidden; pinned with the ☆ beside a statistic in the Inspector. The mean is the plain mean of the samples
  • A template is also a profile: its at-a-glance numbers, its instruments and its pinned searches (☆ beside the signal list's search box: a chip under it, kept in the session and the template, with Undo). The built-in ArduPilot, MAVLink and PX4 templates bring theirs (max altitude, max speed, battery used, lowest voltage…; ATT, VIBE, GPS, BAT…); a template you save keeps yours

docs.title: Live instruments
docs.text: • Checks ▸ Instruments: big readouts of each chosen signal's latest value at the time (while live: the newest data from a MAVLink link, data sent from Python or a file being written) and the attitude indicator with heading, altitude and ground speed; a reading that stopped arriving says how old it is; tiles added and removed with Undo; a template brings its own

docs.title: Test-bench example
docs.text:
• A pump on a test bench on the welcome screen (examples/bench/pump_run_07.parquet): phases as a state, units, a 0.2 s pressure spike, a 2 s gap and a motor temperature that creeps over its limit. Its checks.json runs in CI: signalviewer-cli check examples/bench/pump_run_07.parquet --checks examples/bench/checks.json (2 of 4 checks fail, on purpose; exit code 1). The app runs the same file: a checks file beside a recording (<name>.checks.json, or checks.json in its folder) shows in Checks as its own card with the CLI's verdict, and counts in the Checks pill above the plots
  • An example whose data no built-in view fits opens with Quick look

docs.title: Flight log (ArduPilot)
docs.text: • The Log button of the side rail works while a flight log is open (.bin, .tlog, .ulg; a red dot when the log has errors) and is greyed otherwise; nothing changes for CSV / MAT. Events: messages, flight-mode changes, events (ARMED…) and errors in time order, coloured by severity (from the text: PreArm / low / glitch → warning; fail / crash / EKF variance → error), search and filters; click an event → the cursor goes there and every plot scrolls to it; the row in force at the cursor is highlighted. On the plots: warnings and errors (or every message, or none) as markers along the top, text when there is room, full text on hover; events at the same moment are merged. Parameters: search (prefix in bold), changed in flight with each change clickable (20 → 25 @ 11 s), not default (when the log records defaults; the default is shown crossed out), differences against another open log; copy or save as .param (NAME,VALUE, for Mission Planner / MAVProxy) exactly the rows shown

docs.title: Health check
