docs.text: • Checks (for a log: its health check): vibration, accelerometer clipping, GPS satellites / HDop / fix, battery (below BATT_LOW_VOLT / BATT_CRT_VOLT for BATT_LOW_TIMER seconds, the resting voltage with BATT_FS_VOLTSRC = 1), EKF variances (FS_EKF_THRESH), motors at full output and motor imbalance (the motor outputs from SERVOn_FUNCTION, named by motor number), board power, errors / warnings in the log. Each finding: a sentence, the moment (click → cursor), the stretches (click → zoom with both cursors on it), Plot (its signals in a new tab). Works for .bin, .tlog and .ulg

docs.title: Filter review, step response, hardware (1.21)
docs.text:
• IMU batch sampler (INS_LOG_BAT_MASK): ISBH / ISBD become ISBD[i].GyrX … AccZ at the sensor's own rate; with INS_LOG_BAT_OPT 4 (or 2) the samples after the filters are …Post. Their spectrum (FFT / Welch) is taken per burst and averaged ("averaged over N bursts") instead of bridging the pauses between bursts
  • Filters on an FFT plot (or the ArduPilot · Filter review template): the harmonic notches' lines at the centre frequencies the log recorded (FTN / FTNS / FCN, else INS_HNTCH_FREQ) × the harmonics of INS_HNTCH_HMNCS (and INS_HNTC2_*), the gyro low-pass (INS_GYRO_FILTER), and for a gyro before the filters a dashed line: its spectrum after them, estimated with ArduPilot's own filter coefficients - as ArduPilot's Filter Review
  • Step response plot type (and a tab of ArduPilot · Rates (PID)): signals in pairs (setpoint, measured - RATE.RDes, RATE.R); the loop's response to a step estimated from the flight by Wiener deconvolution over 2-second windows, averaged; rise time, overshoot and settling; over the cursors' region when they are on; needs 40 Hz or more (fast attitude / PID logging) - as ArduPilot's PID Review and PID-Analyzer
  • Checks ▸ Hardware: the board and firmware (boot messages), frame, ESC protocol, loop rate, each IMU / compass / barometer decoded from its device id (chip, bus, address), GPS and battery monitor types; Copy for a forum post - as ArduPilot's Hardware Report

docs.title: Built-in views
docs.text: • Templates (file panel or the Recordings bar): ArduPilot (attitude, rates, vibration + IMU spectrogram, battery & power, GPS with the track on a map, motors & RC, altitude, EKF), MAVLink and PX4 views. Signals matched without units / instance numbers, with alternatives (EKF3 / EKF2); plots the log cannot fill are left out. User templates match the same flexible way

docs.title: Live MAVLink
docs.text:
• Live ▸ MAVLink: UDP (udpin:127.0.0.1:14550 for SITL / MAVProxy / a forwarding ground station, udpin:0.0.0.0:14550 from another computer), TCP (tcp:127.0.0.1:5760) or a serial port (listed, with its baud rate)
  • The link is recorded to a .tlog in ~/.signalviewer/recordings, opened like any file and followed by live mode; Disconnect keeps it
  • Only listens by default; Ask the vehicle to send data acts as a minimal ground station (heartbeat + one request for all streams)
  • A pill next to Live shows messages per second and turns red when the link goes quiet

docs.title: A folder of recordings
docs.text:
• Sweeps ▸ Data ▸ From a folder of recordings… (also Sweeps' Open ▾, Ctrl+K and Investigate ▸ Runs matrix ▸ Summarize a folder): one row per recording of a folder - the same measures in each (max / min / mean / rms / final… of a signal, optionally only where a condition holds) and parameters from the file name ({vehicle}_{date}); read one file at a time (memory: one file's), any format, sub-folders not included
  • A measures.json beside the recordings (the Runs matrix's Save measures: {"measures": [...], "pattern": "..."}) is used at once; without one, the folder's first recording opens with the Runs matrix to define the measures on it, and its Summarize a folder remembers the folder. The same file runs from the command line: signalviewer-cli summarize <folder> --measures measures.json
  • The table opens in Sweeps with a recording column: tick rows and Open in Recordings opens them together (Compare-ready); a set's detail opens its runs' recordings
  • The welcome card A folder of recordings (examples/folder_of_flights, ten flights of two copters with its measures.json): X8-A's vibration grows flight after flight (18 → 67), X8-B's battery drops on its last flight

docs.title: Map
docs.text:
• One Map (1.26): the earth with its terrain; its bar's camera Free · On the object on a chosen object (2026-11-16: only these two - On the object turns around it with a drag and goes nearer with the wheel, all the way to sitting on it; a double-click on an object, F, Ctrl+K Map camera; arrows look around it; a session saved with an earlier camera opens Free, or On the object when it followed one), + / − / fit, Relation, Display, ▶ Story; the mouse's latitude / longitude, ground height and distance from the reference (and from the nearest place) in a corner. Without graphics acceleration it is drawn flat and says so. 3D (XYZ) is the other plot type - any three signals on plain 3D axes, not a map.
  • Places (1.26): points (with an icon), lines and areas on every Map, and saved camera views - Places of this session and My places (~/.signalviewer/places.json); right-click Add a place here…, typed positions (decimal or degrees-minutes-seconds), Mark this spot, import .kml / .kmz / .geojson / .csv, export .kml; a click flies there; in the pages, pictures, KML and ACMI (stationary waypoints).
  • The wow (1.26): the sun where it was, sky, soft shadows near the objects, drop lines and discs, the last 10 s brighter, camera flights, the view from the object (On the object, zoomed all the way in), the flight display (attitude, ground speed and altitude tapes), a mini-map, and the error surface between truth and a navigation solution (green → red at the 95th percentile; the flat drawing colours the track). Off in the light mode.
  • Story mode (1.26): the moments that matter (the log's marks, takeoff / landing, highest, fastest, steepest bank, passing a place, the largest error or closest / farthest) played as a guided film in the live page and the app; PDF / Word "The flight in N moments".
  • Settings > Map and objects (1.26): a new object's icon by its class, a new Map's camera and relation box, Always flat, names, track width, model size, m-km / ft-NM, decimal / DMS / MGRS, elevation files, the export rate, the Story - for new things only.
  • The Geo plot (longitude × latitude) on real maps: streets (OpenStreetMap, or Esri), light / dark grey (Esri, with labels); automatic is the offline map (since 1.23; nothing is sent), the online maps are marked ☁ in the Map background picker and an amber Online map sign shows while they are used; Settings ▸ Never use the network (or SV_OFFLINE=1) turns them off, satellite (Esri World Imagery), topographic (OpenTopoMap). Tiles come through the app and are kept on disk (~/.signalviewer/tiles), so places already seen work without internet; without internet the map shows country borders and names (Natural Earth, English / Hebrew). Borders (a background in the Map picker, over the offline map and satellite): country borders with a halo, dashed, and the names, over the satellite photos too - with no internet as well. Track with a halo, start (green) / end (red), the cursor's position, scale bar in metres, the provider's attribution. Wheel = zoom at the pointer, drag = pan, double-click = fit
  • The pointer over a time plot of the same tab shows a faint copy of each object where it was at that moment (on the map; a faint point in 3D) - also with the cursors on; nothing moves the cursor
  • Every object of a recording found by its names (since 1.24) - every prefix with a latitude and a longitude (phys.*, nav.*, gps.*, ins2_*; NED / ENU / ECEF positions too), classed as truth, navigation or receiver - and added at once (one Undo) or chosen, with Why?: which signals, by which rule, what is missing, what almost matched; each object takes its signals from its own prefix only. A line in the file panel offers them when the file opens. Truth is drawn as a line, a navigation solution dashed, a receiver as points
  • An attitude for an object without one: from its motion (heading along the course over ground, pitch from the climb, held below a speed) or borrowed from another object on the same vehicle - its icon outlined, ≈ on its chip
  • Primary and secondary objects (since 1.24): range, horizontal distance, height difference, bearing, relative bearing, closure, time and distance of closest approach, heading difference and aspect at the cursor; their error signals (position, altitude, attitude) and differences over time in NED, ENU, ECEF, latitude / longitude / altitude or along / across the primary's track, velocity differences, all in one click (relate, in the backend); click an object to make it the primary, Shift+click a secondary; Q / X keys in 3D
  • Smooth motion (since 1.24): drag with glide, wheel and + / − zoom, Fit everything, Follow (with an offset by dragging; the N button turns the map with the object and back north), arrow / + / − / F / 0 keys; while playing only what moves is drawn again. The 3D camera On the object, with a short flight between views
  • Export the flight (1.26, a map's or a 3D view's menu; since 1.27 under Save / export): Tacview (.acmi)…, Tacview CSV files (a folder)… (one per object, Model (name) [Colour].csv), Google Earth (.kml)… (a timed track per object when the log has dates). The ACMI's Name is a model Tacview draws (C172, MQ-9, DJI300, AIM-9M, Zodiac, Pickup), the object's name its CallSign; objects with no position are left out and named; the shown places go too.
  • Export for Tacview (.acmi)… (since 1.24, now under Export the flight): the objects as a Tacview ACMI 2.2 text file - position, altitude above sea level and attitude as the 3D view draws them, 10 samples a second, the kind (plane, rotorcraft, ship, ground vehicle, missile), name and nearest Tacview colour
  • Objects whose position is in metres (since 1.25) - NED, ENU or ECEF - are found and added like latitude / longitude ones: tgt.ned.x, nav.x_ned, ship.ecefX, boat.pos.north / east / up; every ArduPilot EKF lane (XKF1[n], NKF1[n]) with its own attitude through the EKF origin (ORGN), PX4 and MAVLink local positions through theirs. The origin is found (the object's own ref_*, a known group, an origin / ref / home / datum group beside it), explained in Why?, and never offered as an object; a row without one opens Advanced… with a suggestion
  • The rings explained and chosen in one place (since 1.25): a tooltip on each ring, ring marks on the chips, and the relation box's first line - Reference, Compared with, ⇄ - the same on the map and in 3D
  • Compare objects… (since 1.25; the relation box's Compare…, Ctrl+K): reference, objects, position / velocity / attitude, values / errors / both, the frame (NED, ENU, ECEF, LLA, track) → a tab per quantity with every line named and coloured by its object, and the errors' statistics on the full data (RMS, mean, largest, 95 %, time of the largest - a click puts the cursor there); copy / CSV. The four earlier actions are one-click presets in it
  • Compare with similar… (since 1.25; a signal's or a group's menu, Ctrl+K): the signals of one file whose names differ in one part (nav1 / nav2 / truth, [0] / [1]) as families - values, errors against a reference member, angle differences wrapped
  • A map leaves the app (since 1.25): Save image (PNG) (this view or all the tracks), Save as HTML (opens offline) - one file with the tracks, a time slider and values on hover - and maps inside reports (PDF, Word, HTML)
  • The whole process from a script (since 1.25): rec.objects(), sv.compare_objects(…), sv.similar(…), sv.map_image / map_html, sv.report; signalviewer-cli objects | compare-objects | compare-similar | map (with --tolerance for pass / fail and JUnit); POST /api/objects/detect | compare | similar - the same numbers as the dialog. See Scripting API and Command line

docs.title: Map backgrounds, height profile, arrows (1.27)
docs.text:
• The Map background picker in the corner of every map (2D and 3D): each background as a picture of the place on screen - Offline (the default), the online maps marked ☁ (greyed out with the reason when Never use the network is on), Borders, Satellite + roads (Esri satellite photos with the roads and their names) and your own maps; opening it downloads nothing
  • My maps (Add a map…): a raster MBTiles file (fully offline) or an XYZ / TMS tile server of your own, in 2D, 3D, exported pictures and offline map pages; Never use the network blocks a server on the internet, not one on this PC or a private address
  • Keep this area offline…: an area's tiles at chosen zooms, the size estimated first, progress, Stop, the kept areas with their size and Delete - only where the map's terms allow it (ground heights, your own servers); OpenStreetMap, Esri and OpenTopoMap forbid bulk downloads and the dialog says so
  • A quieter offline map in both themes (land and water a step off the app's colours, softer relief, roads muted by their order); the camera bar is one glass bar in the top corner, the data box at the bottom corner, nothing covers anything else
  • Height profile (Profile under the map bar's ⋯): the object's height and the ground under it along the distance, for any recording with positions; the cursor's moment marked, a click moves the cursor; coarse ground data is said, with how to get finer (.hgt, or keep the area offline)
  • Arrows along the path: any two signals (north and east components - a wind, a velocity, a force) drawn as arrows along an object's track on the map and in 3D; the file's own pair is offered (an ArduPilot log's estimated wind, a CSV's velocity)

docs.title: Sweeps: a run envelope's results
docs.text: A second work area (the top bar: Recordings · Sweeps) for a table with a row per run - the parameters and scenarios first, the outputs last (CSV, Parquet or Excel, or a folder of them) - and the question which parameters hold in every scenario, and which of them is best? Try it on the example: a drone's roll controller (kp_roll, ki_roll, filter_hz; wind, payload, gusts; roll error, overshoot, energy...), with a second, finer sweep to merge. The same answer on the command line: signalviewer-cli sweep.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
• The five steps of every study (a table or a study file): 1 Data · 2 Columns · 3 Goal · 4 Results · 5 Next runs; each says where it stands, a step that needs a table says so.
  • 1 Data: every table loaded is listed apart in the tables' column (only in Data, resizable; tick to merge, show, export as CSV or as HTML with its parallel plot - its axes, colour, filters and zoom as on screen -, Remove from the study with Undo); the table page by page and sortable (the name column fixed), or every run as a parallel plot (a click on a column's name colours by it; the wheel and + / − zoom, a drag pans, a click on a line shows that run and marks its row in the table). Merge makes a new table from the ticked ones: the rows one under the other (a column some lack is empty there) or side by side on key columns (join), with a source column (its name yours) and duplicate rows removed if wanted, a preview of the rows; the tables merged stay; in a study the navigator chooses the table the next steps work on; each table merged in is an iteration.
  • 2 Columns: each column's role guessed - Parameters, Outputs, Conditions (a set must hold in every combination of them), Identifiers (a run id or a recording), Not used - each explained in its header, with its kind and range; above the table undo / redo, Reset to guessed roles, Template ▾ (save to a JSON file, load - 12 of 14 columns matched, 2 new columns need a role, 1 formula skipped (missing payload_kg), the columns to check marked) and the study's numbers in a row (runs as 640 of 1,922 when conditions are filtered); in the side panel each condition as a folding card (many values: a search, +N more with each value's runs, All / None, a min-max range), Split results by this, the columns that tell nothing marked not used in one click, and new columns - a formula per run (range_m / payload_kg, completing names and functions, the first run's value or what is wrong; conditions and text as well: if(wind > 8, "high", "low"), comparisons - also 0 < x <= 5 - and and / or / not, x in (1, 2), name == "mild", contains(name, "B"), between(x, lo, hi), bins(x, [0, 5, 10]), rank(x), pct(x); a text result is a new condition (a scenario) with its own card, a number one is an output or, when chosen, a condition) or one value per parameter set (min, max, mean, median, P10, P90, spread, count, count_true and share of a condition column - in how many of its runs it held - over all its runs or some conditions), changed and deleted from a list. Table tools (S2): drop every Not used column, keep only the runs where a condition holds, a column's shown name and unit, values fixed by hand - steps of the study (the file never changes, Ctrl+Z, saved with the study); Export the table writes CSV, Parquet or Excel as edited, with a .recipe.json beside it.
  • 3 Goal: one table, a row per output and parameter - at least / at most (a limit is a filter on its column; an output must meet it in every condition; empty = no limit, with how many sets meet each) and what to optimize (minimize / maximize, weights from two objectives, by the worst case; with two or more, ranked by the weighted score or by the Pareto front, then the closest to the ideal, and Show the Pareto front); Ctrl / Shift-click choose several rows and one bar sets them (a value or a % of each column's range); a new column says new; a limit on a column no longer used is said. The count and the best set follow each change. More options: conditions in at least k combinations or in chosen ones (the column found by typing part of its name), and / or, how an output shows per set, Robust to a parameter (± %, ± a value, ± grid steps), several goals compared side by side.
  • 4 Results: Show: Holds ▾ (all, holds, fail, a group) for the table, the lines and the export; Parameter sets · N and All runs · N (how many lines each draws) - the parallel plot filtered as in HiPlot (drag on an axis, Shift-drag for another range; zoom), Keep / Exclude / restore, undo / redo, the goal's axes (rank, score, each objective), Fit to width, export the shown as CSV or the plot as HTML; the sets best first with each condition's worst case and margin, why it fails for a set, columns, sort, Export; Charts - as many as wanted, 1 / 2 / 4 in a row, each duplicated, removed, exported (PNG, a high-resolution PNG, HTML) and in the report or not (lines, points, bubbles, histograms, boxes, a matrix, maps, Pareto - any two objectives, the balanced set starred, each set's Pareto level -, principal components / clusters, a self-organising map); next runs (where to run more - Sharpen the edge, Near the best, Where scenarios disagree, Fill the gaps, Finish what's missing, Is it robust? - on the parameters chosen, the budget shared equally, in proportion to what each found or by hand; exported as CSV, TSV, JSON, MATLAB .m or Python .py; beside them the re-run list you collect from the table and a set's details); the report (HTML, Word, PDF or CSV, with the process: a journal of the final steps, the iterations, Where it comes from; the Charts ticked, next runs' maps, the best set per split value).
  • Split by: one condition's values apart - All together or one value (a set must hold in every combination of the other conditions with it), the best set per value side by side, a group of each value, re-runs kept with their value.

docs.title: Studies, templates and undo
docs.text:
• One Open ▾: New study…, a table, a folder and Open a saved study (a table's .svsweep or a study file, .svstudy.json). New study…: I have results (a table of runs; its columns fill the study's set-up and the answer shows at once) or Start from nothing (Send runs: what varies - ranges, steps and how many values in the first round -, the scenarios and how to run - this PC, a wrapper or the farm's launcher; no outputs, no goal; Send round 1 runs that grid and its results open as a regular table, each next round is aimed)
  • Data's column: Send runs (what varies, scenarios, how to run - how many of the three are filled), the Tables - each table, the tables merged into it and each round the loop has run (new ones marked; a round opens as its table, with the study's roles and goal) - and About this study
  • Results › All systems together (two systems or more, ranked together; a study with one table is ranked on its own)
  • 5 Next runs: the sets proposed from the results (re-run list, suggestions, export to run outside) and Run from the app: what the next round will run (sets × scenarios = runs) or what is still missing, The goal of the loop (asked for here, not before), Run them, Only write the files (for a launcher of your own), Next round, Run until converged, Stop, the progress and the convergence; a table opened alone gets Run from the app… (it makes the study file)
  • Study ▾ → Report of the study…: one offline HTML page of the whole study (what varies, each table's goal and limits, the shared answer with each table's verdict, the rounds run), in the app's language

  • One Undo for all of Sweeps: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change, in a table's question or in the study's set-up

  • Every change is undone with Ctrl+Z (Ctrl+Y redoes); the open studies are kept and open again where they were; a study is saved as .svsweep; Follow the file reads a table again when it changes.

  • Clear ▾ (beside Study ▾): groups, charts, filters and the re-run list; the goal and the results (the columns stay); start the study over; everything (every study closed after asking - the notice's Undo opens them again).
  • Templates (Study ▾ → Templates…): the roles, goals, maps, table columns, robustness and next runs' choices, applied to another table with the same columns (offered when one fits), exported to a file and imported.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• Send it as one page (Report panel, Save the page (HTML)… - the replay and the HTML report are one page since RV8, the report's text below the plots when written; Ctrl+K Send this view as a replay page: the tab alone): one HTML page that opens in any browser offline, on the moment shown - one cursor for every plot and map (a click on a plot or the page's timeline), Play (Space, ×0.5 - ×30) with the plots following, one zoom for every time plot, the log's errors / warnings, the findings and the notes as marks, #t= in the address keeps a moment, a Made with Signal Viewer line; Open it shows it in the browser (1.25)
  • Preview in the app
  • Interactive offline HTML - one live page (1.26): one time bar for every plot, the map and the 3D view (Play, the log's marks); each plot keeps its zoom and statistics
  • The 3D view in reports: live in HTML (three.js, offline; its picture without WebGL), a picture in PDF / Word / PNG; its own offline HTML from its ⋯ menu
  • A plot that cannot go into a report (a video, occurrences) is listed with the reason, not left out
  • A single plot: PNG, a high-resolution PNG for a report (twice the pixels), SVG, or an interactive page (HTML)
  • PDF
  • Word
  • Per-plot captions, include/exclude, report language

docs.title: A Sweeps table from recordings
docs.text:
• The Runs matrix (Investigate › Runs matrix; Sweeps › Data › From the open recordings…; a folder: From a folder of recordings…): a row per open run with its measures - a signal by name and max / min / mean / RMS / std / range / first / final / the value at a time / time of max or min / overshoot / settling time, optionally only where a condition holds - the values shown at once for every open run (define them on one run, see them right), parameters from the file names (kp_{kp}_wind_{wind}), the conditions' counts or durations. Open in Sweeps makes it a Sweeps table (the recording of each row kept: Open its recording from a set).
  • Summarize a folder → Sweeps…: the same measures for every recording in a folder, read one at a time in the background without opening them (progress, Cancel, memory of one file); cli.py summarize does the same from a script (Save measures… writes the file it reads).
  • A run's recording by its number: a Sweeps table without a column of file names - in a set's details, Where are the runs' recordings? takes a folder and a name made from the row (flight_{run_id}.bin; {column} is that column, * anything; empty: the name ends with the run's number). The set's runs then open in Recordings; the folder is looked in only when a set is shown, and a missing file is named. Saved with the study.

docs.title: Export a part of a recording
docs.text: • Export recording… (the top bar's ⤓ beside Save; Ctrl+K): the signals in the plots on screen or every signal of the file; all the time, what the plots show, between the cursors, or only where a condition holds (with seconds before and after; a Segment column numbers the stretches); as recorded (the fastest signal's samples) or one time base at a chosen rate - values linear, states held, a low-pass first when the rate goes down (anti-alias, can be turned off); time from 0 if wanted. CSV, Parquet, MATLAB .mat or HDF5 (by the name's extension), units in the header / attributes, and <file>.export.json beside it saying what was taken. Every file opens again in the app. One file, or one per open file (the same signals by name). The plot's Export data (CSV) and cli.py export write through the same code.

docs.title: Batch reports
docs.text: • python cli.py report --template T --out DIR files… – one report per file (HTML, PDF or Word, English or Hebrew) with the same template matching and drawing as the app (the matching lives in one place, backend/svcore/templates.py); files that cannot be read or have none of the template's signals are skipped and named; --template takes a name, an id or a template .json

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
• Save / open, autosave and restore
  • Locate missing files when a session is opened

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
• For any file type: the file panel shows the templates that fit the open files, All templates… and Save as template… (once something is plotted the list is folded to one line - click it to unfold); the Recordings bar's Templates ▾ menu opens a template or collection, saves one, or starts a collection (also in the command palette and a tab's right-click menu). The layout and its signals are stored by name; opening a template applies one to the open files in a new tab — to one file, or to every file that has the signals
  • Missing signals are listed
  • A chip in the file panel opens its template in one click when it is clear which file goes where (right-click: the library)
  • A template is a set of tabs (one tab, or many); a collection includes other templates by reference (opening it opens all their tabs, and it follows their changes; loops are refused). Signals are stored by name with the file they come from: the files a template uses are found from its tabs when it is saved (one per source file, named after it; shown as a read-only list). When a template is opened, an open file with the same name is used; if it is not open, the open file with most of its signals is suggested (12 of 14 signals) - or choose another, all files that fit (overlaid), or Open run_a.csv when the original still exists. Choose which tabs to open (All / None; a template's default tabs - Opened by default in the editor - are checked; a chip of a template with several tabs asks, unless Settings ▸ Opening a template says Default tabs); right after a file loads only the default tabs open (the built-in full reviews: Attitude and Flight) and the others wait in +N more from ▾ beside the tab bar's +; plots the files cannot fill are left out and named. Library (Recordings bar → Templates): grouped list (my templates, any file, ArduPilot, MAVLink, PX4, comparisons) with how well the open files fit, search, details; New from the current tab, from all open tabs, or as a collection; edit name, description, group, tabs (a new template starts with the current tab under a relevant name; + Add a tab… lists the open tabs, those already in the template marked added, plus all remaining tabs; rename, reorder, remove) and included templates; built-in templates are copied to my templates to change them; delete your own templates (the trash icon in the list, right-click, the details or the editor; built-in ones cannot be deleted); export / import (.json) and open the folder: map / 3D objects are kept in templates by signal names like the plots' signals; built-in Flight on the map & 3D templates for ArduPilot, MAVLink and PX4 (PX4's attitude from its quaternion), and Position on the map & 3D for any file with latitude / longitude (found by their names; suggested only then); every template is its own JSON file, by default in ~/.signalviewer/templates – Change folder… keeps them in any folder you choose (a shared drive, say; the current templates are copied there, and the app looks for templates there from then on), Default folder goes back (the old templates.json is converted). For any file: Quick look (each signal in its own plot, 4 per tab) and Compare open files (every signal two or more files share, overlaid)
  • A chip in the file panel opens its template in one click when it is clear which file goes where (right-click: the library)

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: • info, export (.csv / .mat), report (one per file from a template), check (limits as pass / fail: whole run, time window or a state's stretches; the limits saved in a template; exit code 0 / 1 / 2; JUnit XML), compare (each run against a golden run, tolerances per signal, a share of samples allowed outside, alignment by cross-correlation, JUnit XML), sweep (a run envelope's results table: how many parameter sets hold in every scenario, the best of them; a study saved by the app; exit code 0 / 1 / 2), validate (the numerical validation), readers, templates

docs.title: General
docs.text:
• Progress + cancel for long operations
  • Undo/Redo
  • Command palette
  • Hebrew/English with RTL
  • Light/dark
  • WCAG AA contrast
  • Text size 100–125 %
  • Live mode with follow last N seconds

docs.title: Error details
docs.text:
• Help → Copy error details: the version, the system and the end of the app's own log, to paste into a bug report
  • Help → Report a problem…: the same details copied, and the bug report form opened in your browser
  • Errors in the server, background jobs, threads and the interface are written to ~/.signalviewer/logs/signalviewer.log (1 MB × 4; SV_LOG_DIR moves it)
  • An unexpected server error shows a readable message
  • Nothing is sent anywhere

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: Key Action Ctrl+K Command palette (commands and signals) Ctrl+O Open files Ctrl+P Quick open: recent files, recent and favourite folders Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+O Save / open session Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undo / Redo Ctrl+PageUp / Ctrl+PageDown Previous / next tab Space Cursor on/off D Two cursors ← → (Shift = ×10) Move the cursor from one recorded sample to the next (no interpolation; only the mouse interpolates) 1–9 Select plot R Reset zoom (to the axis limits, if set) N Note at the cursor F5 / Ctrl+R Refresh all files Backspace Previous zoom P Play / pause (the timeline) Home / End The timeline: start / end of the recording Ctrl + / Ctrl − / Ctrl 0 Text size ? Keyboard shortcuts Delete Remove the selected signal from its plot

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: The welcome screen (1.27) – a demo for every area, grouped: Recordings, Sweeps The smart-sweep demo – the next runs converge on the full grid's optimum with ~64× fewer runs One set of gains for three drones – the values that hold in every table, why the others fail, the runs of a value All runs – a line per run across the parameters, each scenario and the outputs What changed first – every signal that left its usual range, in time order, each with its file, the likeliest cause first The process in brief – every report opens with the data, what was checked, what it shows and the conclusion Replay page (1.25) – the tab as one page to send: map and plots on one cursor, Play, the log's marks Send it as one page – from the Report panel; two cursors with Δ in every chip, the plots' window on the timeline Map + 3D – offline map with terrain, roads and place names; 3D view with the vehicle and a live data box 3D terrain – the bundled elevation (the Jordan rift really is below sea level) Compare – similarity list, overlay of every run, RMS Δ / max Δ / correlation per run Comparison table – every shared signal, coloured by how different it is Built-in views – ArduPilot attitude with the flight mode drawn on every plot Vibration – VIBE levels, clipping and an IMU spectrogram Health check – each finding with its moment, its stretches and a Plot button Events – messages, modes and errors; click one to put the cursor there Formulas – autocomplete, argument help and did you mean…? Templates – built-in and your own, matched to the open files Smart start – the first log gets a suggested view and its worst findings, each a click from its moment Same segment, every run – the files' segments lined up at 0, in a tab named after the segment Live MAVLink – UDP / TCP / serial, recorded as it arrives; only listens unless asked Motor orders – 1×, 2×, 3× the rotation rate and the blade pass, over the spectrum's window Coordinate frames – LLA → NED and more, previewed in a plot per axis, created as one group Every signal at a glance – its unit, rate and a small picture in the file list Dark theme עברית – full Hebrew interface, right to left Sweeps – which parameter sets hold in every condition; the goal as one table: limits on columns and what to optimize, the count and the best set live Sweeps: the data – each table apart, merged into a new one by rows or on key columns, with a source column Split by a condition – the best set for each payload, with the same goal Several objectives – ranked by the Pareto front; the balanced set starred Many signals – the legend in a column beside the plot, the values aligned Track by mode – the map track in the mode lane's colours, with a key A flight at a glance – the track coloured by mode, the vehicle in 3D, roll and vibration at a finding Judge a run (1.23) – the model as the golden run, the differences with the tolerance, the verdict per file

docs.title: Install, build and run from source
docs.text:
Download: the latest release. On Windows take SignalViewer-Setup-X.Y.Z.exe (installs for you only, no administrator rights); to run without installing, the …-Windows-x64-portable.zip (extract, double-click Signal Viewer.bat). Linux and macOS: the -portable.7z for your system.

With Python (3.9 or newer): pip install signalviewer, then signalviewer starts the app - with every reader and report (pip install "signalviewer[desktop]" for its own window instead of the browser). The light install: pip install signalviewer-lite (about 350 MB instead of 760) is the core - CSV, MATLAB v5, ArduPilot .bin, CAN, binary layouts, every plot and analysis, HTML reports - and the rest are extras: [parquet] (also a faster CSV reader), [hdf5] (.h5, MATLAB v7.3), [mavlink] (.tlog, live MAVLink), [px4] (.ulg), [ros] (.mcap), [reports] (PDF, Word, images), [desktop], [all]; a file that needs one says which. Both install the same signalviewer Python package: install one of them, not both. signalviewer-cli and import signalviewer read and export recordings from scripts. rec.signal("ATT.Roll") finds ATT.Roll [deg] (the unit may be left out), and signalviewer.show(t, {"alt": alt}) sends arrays from a notebook into the open app.

docs.title: First start: Windows and macOS warnings
docs.text:
The packages are not code-signed yet, so the first start may be stopped once:

  • Windows (Windows protected your PC, SmartScreen): More info → Run anyway. Shown for the installer and for SignalViewer.exe from the portable package, once per version.
  • macOS ("SignalViewer" cannot be opened or is damaged): macOS marks files that came from the internet. Remove the mark from the extracted folder once, in Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /path/to/SignalViewer, then start SignalViewer in it (or right-click it → Open → Open). The macOS package is for Apple silicon (M1 and later).

docs.title: Building the packages
docs.text:
Nothing needs the internet at run time. The installer, the portable folder and the single file contain Python, every library, the UI with its fonts, the report assets and the icon. Verified by running the built app with no network interface at all.

Build command (Windows) Result When build.bat installer dist\SignalViewer-Setup-1.28.0.exe Recommended. One file; installs for the current user (no admin), Start-menu and desktop icons, Open with for data files, uninstaller build.bat portable dist\SignalViewer-portable.zip Unzip anywhere and run SignalViewer.exe (fast start) build.bat onefile dist\SignalViewer.exe A single file to copy; starts a few seconds slower (it unpacks itself each time) build_windows_portable.bat (Windows) / python tools/make_windows_portable.py dist\SignalViewer-Windows-portable.7z Windows portable build on a Windows PC: double-click the .bat (needs Python 3.8+ with pip and internet, once, only to build). Downloads the official embeddable Python + the Windows builds of the libraries; the result needs no Python and no internet. 7z (about 80 MB instead of 126 MB as zip): made with 7-Zip when installed, else with the py7zr library fetched once; Windows 11 opens .7z in Explorer, Windows 10 needs 7-Zip. --format zip for a zip, --keep-folder keeps the assembled folder, --clean forces a fresh download, --build-ui rebuilds the web UI first (Node.js; done automatically when the UI sources are newer than the built UI) tools/make_windows_portable.sh (Linux/macOS) dist/SignalViewer-Windows-portable.7z Builds the same Windows package without a Windows PC (runs the same Python builder; options are passed on) build.bat wheels wheels\ On a connected PC: downloads the libraries once, so the build itself can run on an offline PC

The installer needs Inno Setup 6 on the BUILD PC only (free).

Windows window engine. The app window uses Microsoft Edge WebView2 (built into Windows 11 and updated Windows 10). If it is missing (e.g. an old offline Windows 10 LTSC), the app opens in the local browser instead — still with no internet — says why in the page (and in the log), and stops by itself 5 minutes after its last tab was closed (or a minute after the tab says it is closing; never while a file is still being read). The portable package unblocks its own DLLs that Windows marked as downloaded, which used to send it to the browser every time.

The UI is built for Chromium 87 / Firefox 78 and newer (frontend/vite.config.ts, MIN_CHROMIUM in run.py). An offline computer often keeps an older WebView2: the app then opens in a newer Edge or Chrome as a window of its own (--app, with a profile of its own in ~/.signalviewer/browser-profile), else in Firefox, else it shows a message box with what to install (the Evergreen Standalone Installer of the WebView2 runtime). If the page still does not start, the page itself says why instead of staying blank. Safe graphics (--safe-graphics, the Signal Viewer (safe graphics) shortcut) draws without the graphics card - for a white or black window on virtual machines, remote desktop or old drivers; the 3D view still works, drawn by the processor.

Ready-made packages (no Python and no installation needed, except the Windows installer itself) are built by the GitHub Actions workflow in .github/workflows/build.yml for Windows (x64: the installer, a portable .zip and .7z), Linux (x64) and macOS (Apple silicon): run it manually (Actions → build → Run workflow) and download them from the run's artifacts, or push a tag such as v1.0.0 to also get a draft Release with every file and a "which file?" note. Windows: the embeddable-Python package described above; Linux / macOS: the PyInstaller folder (SignalViewer.spec) - extract it and run SignalViewer/SignalViewer.

Build it yourself: build.bat (Windows) or ./build.sh (Linux / macOS) → dist/SignalViewer[.exe].

docs.title: Run from source
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python run.py              # native window (pywebview), or the browser if pywebview is missing
python run.py --browser    # always use the browser
python run.py flight.bin   # open files (or a .svsession) - in the app that is already running, if there is one

The UI is already built (frontend/dist). When the UI code is newer than that build (after a pull, a patch or an edit), run.py builds it once by itself - Node.js needed - into frontend/.local-dist (ignored by git; the tracked frontend/dist is not touched) and serves that; the next start sees it is current and starts at once. python run.py --build forces a build, --no-build (or SV_NO_BUILD=1) never builds. Without Node.js it says so and shows the last build. For working on the UI:

python run.py --port 8765 --no-open   # backend
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev      # dev server with hot reload, proxies /api to port 8765
npm run build    # rebuilds frontend/dist

Tests:

python -m pytest backend/tests          # ~980 server tests (incl. damaged copies of every format)
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
python -m pytest tests/e2e              # ~320 browser tests, the whole suite in one run (~10-15 min)
python -m pytest tests/e2e/test_features.py    # or one file: one test per catalog feature
cd backend && mypy --config-file ../pyproject.toml app svcore signalviewer   # type check
python tools/benchmark.py big.csv       # performance against the targets (results in docs/)
python tools/benchmark.py --synthetic   # the plot / offset / memory / live benchmarks, on generated data

docs.title: מדריך: לברר מה השתבש
docs.text:
עשר דקות עם כלי החקירה על שתי ריצות שנבנו לשם כך, עם תשובה ידועה.

במסך הפתיחה ← לברר מה השתבש (חקירה) (או לפתוח את examples/investigate/heavy_payload.csv ואת light_payload.csv). אותה משימת רחפן, פעמיים, דרך שלוש משבי רוח: עם מטען של 2.4 ק״ג ועם 1.2 ק״ג. בריצה הכבדה הגלגול יוצא מהערך הרצוי שלוש פעמים; בקלה הוא מחזיק. למה?

(הקבצים נבנו כך שהתשובה ידועה – ראו בסוף.)

docs.title: 1. לראות
docs.text:
1. מסתכלים על הפס שמעל הגרפים: ארבעת שלבי הריצה ושלושה דגלים אדומים – Motor3 שטוח בגבול שלו, ב-AUTO. מעבר עכבר על אחד; בריצה הקלה (בוחרים אותה בפס) אין אף אחד. שמים Roll ו-DesRoll של הריצה הכבדה בגרף. שלוש קפיצות, בערך ב-38, 63 ו-91 ש׳.
  2. קליק ימני על Mode ברשימת הסיגנלים ← רצועה בכל הגרפים בלשונית: מצב הטיסה כפס צבעוני מיושר לגרפים של הלשונית. מעבר עכבר על הפס: המצב שם והמקטע שלו. שלוש הקפיצות ב-AUTO.

docs.title: 2. לתת שם
docs.text:
1. d (שני סמנים) ומקיפים את הקפיצה הראשונה (בערך 38.4 – 39.3 ש׳).
  2. בסרגל שמעל הקטע: מצא דומים. לוח החקירה נפתח עם תנאי שכבר נכתב מהבחירה, על הסיגנל הכי חריג בתוכה (לא משנה איזה גרף פעיל): בערך Roll > 9.86. כותבים אותו פשוט: abs(Roll - DesRoll) > 5, בשם שגיאת גלגול. המספר מופיע תוך כדי הקלדה: 3 מקטעים (כולם בריצה הכבדה – מעבר עכבר על המספר: 0 בקלה).
  3. שמירה. המקטעים מוצללים בגרפים. קליק על השם, או ] / [, עובר מאחד לבא.

docs.title: 3. להסתכל על כולם
docs.text:
1. מתחת לרשימה: המקטעים של שגיאת גלגול – טבלה, שורה לכל מקטע. בוחרים Roll, ‏max: בערך אותו דבר כל פעם.
  2. יחד בלשונית חדשה: שלושת המקטעים של הסיגנל זה על זה, מיושרים להתחלה. קודם בוחרים Motor3 בטבלה ולוחצים שוב: מנוע 3 עומד על 2000 (הגבול שלו) בכל אחד.
  3. מה שונה בפנים: ‏Roll, ‏Vibe_Z, ‏Motor3 ו-Wind רחוקים מהרמה הרגילה שלהם בתוך המקטעים. שונה – עוד לא סיבה.

docs.title: 4. מה בא קודם
docs.text:
1. קליק על השורה של המקטע הראשון (שני הסמנים עליו), ואז מה השתנה? בסרגל.
  2. החיפוש הוא בכל הסיגנלים של heavy_payload.csv: הקובץ של האירוע, לא רק מה שעל הגרפים. הסדר: Wind (בערך ‎−0.44 ש׳), Vibe_Z (‎−0.3), Motor3 (‎−0.22), ‏Motor1, ‏Roll (‎−0.02). הקווים המקווקווים בגרפים הם הרגעים האלה. (Battery_V זז עם הזרם של המנועים.) מתחת לכל סיגנל: הריצה הקלה באותו זמן. Wind, ‏Vibe_Z ו-Motor3 עולים גם שם; Roll: בלי שינוי. כלומר המשב ותגובת המנוע לבדם לא מספיקים – שלב 12 מראה מה שונה. בלוג עם הרבה סיגנלים: מקלידים בסינון, או מוציאים שורה או קבוצה שלמה ב-× שלה (הקווים המקווקווים יוצאים איתה).
  3. מסמנים Motor3 ו-Roll ← השהיה בין שני המסומנים: Roll מגיב בערך 120 ms אחרי Motor3. הצג מיושר מזיז את Roll בגרף הפעיל כך ששתי הצורות נפגשות.

docs.title: 5. לבדוק מול הריצה השנייה
docs.text:
1. שמים את Motor3 של הריצה הקלה ליד זה של הכבדה: אותם משבים, אבל מנוע 3 נשאר מתחת ל-2000 – יש לו מרווח. Motor3 > 1990 כתנאי: 3 מקטעים בכבדה, 0 בקלה.
  2. ריצות × תנאים (מתחת לתנאים): שורה לכל ריצה – Payload_kg (‏2.4 / 1.2, נמצא לבד: יש לו ערך אחד לאורך כל הריצה) – ועמודה לכל תנאי: שגיאת גלגול 3 / 0, רוויה של מנוע 3 ‏3 / 0. קליק על 3: הריצה הכבדה במקטע הראשון שלה.

docs.title: 5½. שגיאות והטיסה הבאה
docs.text:
• שני קווים בגרף (X של מחשב הטיסה ליד ה-X האמיתי; אחד לכל גרף ב-▾ שליד הצגה בגרף מכניס סט כזה): ⋯ ← שגיאה בכל גרף עם שני קווים פותח את השגיאות עם RMS, השגיאה הגדולה ביותר ומתי, ואת מצב הטיסה שבו היא הכי גרועה כשיש כזה שבולט.
  • שומרים תבנית תוך כדי חקירה: היא שומרת את התנאים. פותחים אותה על הקובץ של הטיסה הבאה, ו-ריצות × תנאים סופר אותם שם מיד.

docs.title: 6. לכתוב את זה
docs.text:
1. ב-Inspector נותנים להערות סטטוס: הרוויה – תקלה, ניחוש שלא החזיק (למשל "הסוללה צונחת קודם") – השערה שנפסלה. כל אחת שומרת את התצוגה שבה נמצאה (⌖).
  2. לוח החקירה ← הצעדים עד כה: מה עשית, לפי הסדר. מורידים סימון ממה שהדוח לא צריך.
  3. לוח הדוח ← לכלול את החקירה ← תצוגה מקדימה: ממצאים עם הגרפים שלהם, ההשערה שנפסלה, הצעדים, התנאים לכל ריצה ואיך לשחזר – ואחריהם הגרפים שלך.

התשובה: המשב דורש יותר דחף ממנוע 3; עם המטען הכבד הוא כבר קרוב לגבול, נכנס לרוויה, והגלגול לא מוחזק – כ-0.1–0.15 ש׳ אחר כך. המטען הקל משאיר מרווח, ואותם משבים לא עושים כלום. מה הכלים נתנו: איפה (התנאי), כמה פעמים (3 מתוך 3 משבים, רק בכבדה), מה היה שונה (מנוע 3 בגבול), ובאיזה סדר (רוח ← רעידות ← רוויה ← גלגול).

docs.title: איך הקבצים נבנו
docs.text: python tools/make_investigation_demo.py כותב אותם מחדש. כל משב נבנה בסדר הזה: רוח, רעידות 0.1 ש׳ אחריה, רוויה של מנוע 3 0.1 ש׳ אחרי זה (רק בכבדה), והגלגול עונה על מה שהמנוע לא נתן 0.15 ש׳ אחר כך. שום דבר אחר בקבצים לא קשור לשגיאת הגלגול.

docs.title: Tutorial: find out what went wrong
docs.text:
Ten minutes with the Investigate tools on two runs made for it, with a known answer.

The welcome screen → find out what went wrong (Investigate) opens them (or open examples/investigate/heavy_payload.csv and light_payload.csv). The same quadcopter mission flown twice through three wind gusts: with a 2.4 kg payload and with 1.2 kg. In the heavy run the roll leaves its set point three times; in the light one it holds. Why?

(The files were built so the answer is known - see the end.)

docs.title: 1. See it
docs.text:
1. Look at the strip above the plots: the run's four phases and three red flags - Motor3 flat at its limit, in AUTO. Hover one; the light run (pick it in the strip) has none. Put Roll and DesRoll of the heavy run in a plot. Three bumps, around 38, 63 and 91 s.
  2. Right-click Mode in the signal list → Lane on every plot of this tab: the flight mode as a coloured band lined up with the tab's plots. Hover the band: the mode there and its stretch. All three bumps are in AUTO.

docs.title: 2. Name it
docs.text:
1. Press d (two cursors) and put them around the first bump (about 38.4 – 39.3 s).
  2. On the bar above the span: Find similar. The Investigate panel opens with a condition already written from your selection, on the signal most unusual inside it (whichever plot is active): Roll > 9.86 or so. Write it plainly instead: abs(Roll - DesRoll) > 5, name it Roll error. The count shows while you type: 3 stretches (all in the heavy run - hover the count: 0 in the light one).
  3. Save. The stretches are shaded on the plots. Click the name, or press ] / [, to go from one to the next.

docs.title: 3. Look at all of them
docs.text:
1. Under the list: Stretches of Roll error - a table, one row per stretch. Pick Roll, max: about the same each time.
  2. Together in a new tab: the three stretches of the signal on top of each other, lined up at their start. Switch to Motor3 in the table first, then press it again: motor 3 sits at 2000 (its limit) in every one.
  3. What differs inside: Roll, Vibe_Z, Motor3 and Wind are far from their usual level inside the stretches. Different, not yet cause.

docs.title: 4. What came first
docs.text:
1. Click the first stretch's row (both cursors on it), then What changed? on the bar.
  2. It looks at All signals of heavy_payload.csv - the file of the event, not only what is on the plots. The order: Wind (about −0.44 s), Vibe_Z (−0.3 s), Motor3 (−0.22 s), Motor1, Roll (−0.02 s). The dashed lines on the plots are those moments. (Battery_V moves with the motors' current.) Under each signal: the light run at the same time. Wind, Vibe_Z and Motor3 rise there too; Roll: no change. So the gust and the motor's answer are not enough on their own - step 12 shows what is different. On a log with many signals: type in the filter, or take a row or a whole group out with its × (the dashed lines go with it).
  3. Tick Motor3 and Roll → Lag between the two picked: Roll follows Motor3 by about 120 ms. Show aligned shifts Roll on the active plot so the two shapes meet.

docs.title: 5. Check it against the other run
docs.text:
1. Open the light run's Motor3 next to the heavy one's: the same gusts, but motor 3 stays below 2000 - it has headroom. Motor3 > 1990 as a condition: 3 stretches heavy, 0 light.
  2. Runs × conditions (under the conditions): a row per run - Payload_kg (2.4 / 1.2, found by itself: it holds one value the whole run) - and a column per condition: Roll error 3 / 0, Motor3 saturated 3 / 0. Click the 3: the heavy run at its first stretch.

docs.title: 5½. Errors and the next flight
docs.text:
• Two lines in a plot (a flight computer's X beside the true X; One into each plot in the ▾ beside Plot them puts a set of them in): ⋯ → Error in every plot with two lines opens their errors with RMS, the largest error and when, and the flight mode where it is worst when one stands out.
  • Save a template while investigating: it keeps your conditions. Open it on the next flight's file and Runs × conditions counts them there straight away.

docs.title: 6. Write it up
docs.text:
1. In the Inspector, give your notes a status: the saturation Fault, a guess that did not hold (say "the battery sags first") Rejected hypothesis. Each keeps the view it was found in (⌖).
  2. Investigate panel → Steps so far: what you did, in order. Untick what the report does not need.
  3. Report panel → Include the investigation → Preview: findings with their plots, the rejected hypothesis, the steps, the conditions per run, and how to reproduce it - then your plots.

The answer: the gust needs more thrust from motor 3; with the heavy payload it is already near its limit, saturates, and the roll cannot be held - about 0.1–0.15 s later. The light payload leaves room, so the same gusts do nothing. What the tools gave: where (the condition), how often (3 of 3 gusts, heavy only), what was different (motor 3 at its limit), and in what order (wind → vibration → saturation → roll).

docs.title: How the files were made
docs.text: python tools/make_investigation_demo.py writes them again. It builds each gust in this order: wind, then vibration 0.1 s later, then motor 3 saturating 0.1 s after that (heavy only), and the roll answering what the motor could not give 0.15 s later. Nothing else in the files is related to the roll error.

docs.title: להריץ את המחקר על החווה – מצב Launcher
docs.text: החווה שלכם כבר מריצה סימולציות דרך אפליקציית ה-launcher שלכם: היא מקבלת את תוכנת הסימולציה וקובץ פרמטרים לכל הרצה. Signal Viewer לא מחליף אותה ולא מותקן על מחשבי החישוב. הוא רץ במקום אחד (המחשב הנייד עם הגרסה הניידת, או מחשב ניהול אחד) ומדבר בשפה של ה-launcher. כל מה שנוגע ל-launcher נמצא בבלוק launcher של קובץ המחקר.

docs.title: רשימת הבדיקה (פעם אחת)
docs.text:
1. קחו קובץ פרמטרים אמיתי אחד שה-launcher מקבל (XML או JSON).
  2. החליפו ערכים במצייני מקום: <Kp>1.2</Kp> ← <Kp>{{Kp}}</Kp>. מציין מקום הוא שם עמודה של הטבלה, או {{run_id}}, {{table}}, {{round}}. הערכים מוגנים לפי סוג הקובץ. שמרו ליד המחקר והגדירו params_template_file.
  3. הגדירו submit לשורת הפקודה של ה-launcher, כרשימה (רצה בלי shell). round – פקודה אחת לכל טבלה עם {{params_files}} (קובץ רשימה); run – פקודה לכל הרצה עם {{params_file}}.
  4. הגדירו results – איפה מופיעה תוצאת הרצה, עם {{run_id}}, ובאיזה פורמט (שורת CSV, סדרת זמן עם reduce, JSON עם json_keys, כל קובץ שהאפליקציה קוראת, או פקודת המרה). תוצאה נמצאת לפי run_id, אחרת לפי ערכי הקלט.
  5. הריצו סבב של 3 (next.batch = 3), להריץ אותן בעמודת ההרצה, ובדקו שכל הרצה הופכת לבוצעה.

מה שחוזר נאסף ל-next/round_<k>/collected_<table>.csv: הוסיפו next/round_*/collected_<table>.csv לנתיבים של כל טבלה.

docs.title: באפליקציה ובשורת הפקודה
docs.text:
פותחים את המחקר (Sweeps ← פתיחה ▾ ← פתיחת מחקר שמור): שליחת ריצות בשלב הנתונים אומר איך מריצים ושולח את סבב 1; ריצות הבאות אומר מה הסבב הבא יריץ. להריץ אותן מציג את הפקודה המדויקת פעם אחת בכל הפעלה, מריץ אותה ומראה מתחתיו כל הרצה כנשלחה / בוצעה / נכשלה / חסרה. רק לכתוב את הקבצים כותב את קובצי הפרמטרים של הסבב (‎next/round_<k>/‏) ולא מריץ כלום – ל-launcher שמפעילים בעצמכם.

python -m signalviewer.study submit drones.svstudy.json [--yes]
python -m signalviewer.study wait   drones.svstudy.json             # 0 הכול בוצע, 4 חלק נכשל, 5 פג הזמן
python -m signalviewer.study loop   drones.svstudy.json --max-rounds 5 [--local]

בטיחות: הפקודה באה רק מקובץ המחקר ששמרתם; שום דבר מטבלה או מתוצאה לא הופך לפקודה; אין shell.

לנסות בלי חווה: tools/launcher_mock.py. HPC Pack ישירות: tools/hpc/run_one.ps1 (לא נבדק – לא היה אשכול).

docs.title: Run the study on your farm – Launcher mode
docs.text:
Your farm already runs simulations through your launcher application: it takes the simulation program and a parameters file per run. Signal Viewer does not replace it and is never installed on the compute nodes. It runs in one place (your laptop with the Portable, or one management machine) and speaks the launcher's language:

study ─► one parameters file per run ─► your launcher (sim.exe + params) ─► the farm
  ▲                                                                          │
  └──────────── results, read from where the runs already write them ◄──────┘

Everything about your launcher is in the study's launcher block – there is no launcher-specific code.

docs.title: The owner's checklist (do this once)
docs.text:
1. Take one real parameters file your launcher accepts (XML or JSON).
  2. Replace its values with placeholders: <Kp>1.2</Kp> → <Kp>{{Kp}}</Kp>. A placeholder is a column name of that table (its own name, e.g. {{P_gain}} in a table that calls it so), or {{run_id}}, {{table}}, {{round}}. Values are escaped for the file's format (XML entities in .xml, JSON rules in .json). Save it next to the study and set params_template_file (per table if the tables need different files).
  3. Set submit to the launcher's command line, as a list (it is run without a shell): 
    "submit": ["C:/Tools/Launcher/launcher.exe", "--exe", "{{sim_exe}}", "--list", "{{params_files}}"],
"submit_mode": "round"
    round: one command per table, {{params_files}} is a text file listing that table's parameter files. run: one command per run, with {{params_file}} and {{run_id}}. Also: {{round_dir}}, {{study_dir}}.
  4. Set results to where a run's result appears, with {{run_id}} (default results/{{table}}/{{run_id}}*, relative to the study), and its format: a CSV row, a CSV time series with reduce ({"overshoot": "max(roll)"}), JSON with json_keys ({"overshoot": "out.os"}), any file the app reads (loader), or a converter command that prints one CSV row. A result is found by run_id, else by the run's input values.
  5. Run a round of 3 (set next.batch to 3), Run them in the Next runs step, and check that every run turns done.

What comes back is collected into next/round_<k>/collected_<table>.csv: add next/round_*/collected_<table>.csv to each table's paths and every round's results join the ranking.

Optional: status.failed_glob (a file that marks a failed run), status.timeout_s (per round), local_workers (run the command per run on this PC with N workers – the same path, without a farm).

docs.title: A sweep wrapper on this PC
docs.text:
Between "one run per command" and a farm: a wrapper gets the whole round and runs your simulation once per set of inputs. examples/smart_sweep_demo/sweep_wrapper.py is one to copy (Python, standard library only):

"launcher": { "submit": ["{{study_cli}}", "wrap", "{{study_dir}}/sweep_wrapper.py", "--list", "{{params_files}}",
                         "--sim", "python my_sim.py {params}", "--workers", "4"],
              "submit_mode": "round", "run_as": "wrapper", ... }

run_as: "wrapper" runs the round's command on this PC in the background (the app keeps showing the results as they come). Your simulation reads one JSON file (every input of one run, and "out") and writes one CSV row there. In the app: Send runs → How to run → A wrapper on this PC, and Put the example wrapper beside the study. The same wrapper runs without the app – the inputs as name: values lines, MATLAB-style ranges:

python sweep_wrapper.py --spec grid.txt --out sweep.csv        # grid.txt:  Kp: 0.5, 1, 2:0.5:4   wind: calm, gusty
python sweep_wrapper.py --inputs runs.csv --out sweep.csv      # or a table, one run per row

The smart-sweep demo runs its rounds this way; its folder's README says how to run it by hand.

docs.title: In the app and on the command line
docs.text:
Open the study (Sweeps → Open ▾ → Open a saved study): the Run column on its right says what the next round will run. Run them shows the exact command once per session, runs it, and shows each run under it as submitted / done / failed / missing. Only write the files writes the round's parameter files (next/round_<k>/) and runs nothing - for a launcher you start yourself.

python -m signalviewer.study submit drones.svstudy.json [--yes]     # shows the command; asks unless --yes
python -m signalviewer.study wait   drones.svstudy.json             # 0 all done, 4 some failed, 5 timed out
python -m signalviewer.study loop   drones.svstudy.json --max-rounds 5 [--local]

From the Portable: SignalViewer.exe study … (no Python needed).

Safety: the command comes only from the study file you saved; nothing from a table or a result becomes a command; there is no shell; the app listens only on this computer.

Try it without a farm: tools/launcher_mock.py reads the parameter files (XML or JSON), runs the toy drone model (or --exe your_sim.exe) and writes the results; --fail-rate 0.1 fails some runs on purpose.

HPC Pack directly (not verified – no cluster was available): tools/hpc/run_one.ps1 is one task of a parametric sweep job that writes one run's parameters from a template and runs the simulation.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Interactive HTML reports embed signals longer than 150,000 samples as three min/max levels, so very deep zoom inside the report shows less detail than the app.
  • Copying an image to the clipboard depends on the window's clipboard support; Save image always works.
  • A derived signal whose source file was closed stays in the list, marked, until you remove it.
  • The macOS package is not signed or notarized: after extracting, run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine SignalViewer (or right-click → Open) the first time.
  • Without pyarrow the pandas parser keeps a malformed row that has too few fields (missing values become empty), while pyarrow skips it.
  • The timeline's modes apply to time, X-Y, map and spectrogram plots, not to FFT.
  • In a web browser (not the desktop window) Ctrl+PageUp / Ctrl+PageDown and Ctrl+Tab switch the browser's own tabs; use the All tabs list or Go to tab (Ctrl+K) there.
  • The right value axis follows its data: zooming the values (Shift+drag), panning, the axis limits dialog and linked value axes act on the left axis.
  • Open with (Explorer) is set up by the installer; with the portable packages, open files from the app or SignalViewer file….
  • Installed with pip it opens in the browser (with signalviewer-lite, only the core readers are there until their extras are added - the app says which); pip install "signalviewer[desktop]" gives it its own window (on Linux that needs GTK or Qt).
  • The interactive HTML report lists the notes under its summary; it does not draw them on its plots (the PDF and Word reports do).
  • Columns with a time column of their own keep that column's unit unless it is changed: Time axis… gives them one scale of their own (a time_boot_ms column → ×0.001), the same for all of them - a file whose own time columns are in different units can put only one of those units in seconds.
  • The strip's rows are kept in the session, not in templates; a selection on the strip is made in the strip's run (saved as a condition it applies to every open file).
  • The strip's flags are deliberately few: a signal that is mostly flat (a set point, a counter, a switch) is never flagged as stuck or saturated, nor is anything in the first or last 5% of the run. Files with more than 300 signals are scanned on their first 300.
  • Reports: "Stretches together" (occurrences) plots are not drawn in reports yet; a finding's plot is the time plots of the tab it was found in (up to two) at its view. The journal keeps the last 200 steps; it is saved with the session, not with templates.
  • Runs × conditions works on the open files: a folder of runs is opened (up to 200 files at a time, each read into memory) - for a folder of hundreds, Summarize a folder reads one file at a time into a Sweeps table instead. Parameters come from signals that hold one value and from numbers in file names; a side file of parameters is not read yet.
  • What changed first finds a change in level (beyond 4 times the usual noise, 3 samples in a row); a change only in how a signal oscillates (same level, more shaking) shows only when it pushes samples that far. It reads the usual level well before the span - an event that has been building for longer than that is measured against its own start. Near the start of the file it reads it from whatever is there before the span; with nothing before it, it says so instead of answering.
  • What differs inside the stretches compares means (in units of the spread outside) - a signal that only changes shape, not level, ranks low. The overlay draws the first 200 stretches.
  • Conditions: kept in the session (no shared library yet). A selection is the two cursors - Shift+drag was planned for it, but Shift+drag already zooms the values (T19), so it stays that. Conditions are looked for file by file, on the first signal's samples (other signals: nearest sample).
  • Vector smoothing is a plain centred moving average (no Kalman filter, no outlier rejection); angles and quaternions are not smoothed. The last half-window of a live file is averaged over fewer samples until more arrive.
  • Time axis…: another column as the time for CSV / text, MAT and Parquet; a scale also for HDF5. Flight logs and ROS recordings keep their own clock (only the offset). Cursor, zoom and notes follow the same rows to the new axis only when one file is open and its rows were not re-sorted; with other files open they stay where they are.
  • The window needs an engine from about late 2020 or newer: Microsoft Edge WebView2 / Edge / Chrome 87+, or Firefox 78+. On an older one the app says so instead of starting.
  • CAN: candump logs, Vector ASC (classic CAN lines) and CAN tables in CSV are read; CAN FD lines in ASC files, .blf and MF4 are not. The same id on two buses is decoded as one message.
  • Binary layouts (ICD): fixed fields, bit fields and value names; no checksums (a damaged packet with a good sync and length is read), no arrays or strings inside a payload, no packets whose layout depends on a field.
  • Your own readers run in a process of their own in the app (in Python and the command line they run in the calling process); a reader that never ends is stopped after SV_READER_TIMEOUT (600 s by default). Files read by a reader are reloaded whole in live mode, not appended.
  • A spectrum (FFT, Welch, spectrogram) of a signal with gaps bridges them with straight lines on an even time grid: the frequencies are right, but amplitudes are lower by about the share of time the gaps cover. For exact amplitudes put the two cursors on a stretch without gaps.
  • Telemetry logs (.tlog): messages that carry the autopilot's clock are placed on it (one offset per boot, the median radio delay); messages without it are at their receive time, so they include each packet's radio delay. Live, a boot's offset is learned from its first data and then kept.
  • Sweeps, the goal's table: a limit is at least / at most on a numeric column; a category parameter, conditions in some scenarios only and or goals are set under More options.
  • The legend beside the plot is chosen by an estimate of the names' widths; a plot whose names fit only just may stay above with a third row - Legend ▸ Beside the plot keeps it there. Above the plot, the header may grow once when the values first appear (then it stays until the pointer leaves the plot).
  • Your groups of signals are kept in the session by signal id: a group's signals from a file that is closed are left out of it until the file is open again; templates do not carry groups yet.
  • A made signal's Change the formula… is for formulas; the other operations (derivative, filter…) are made again in Create signals. A changed formula moves the signal to the end of the made signals' list.
  • A coloured map track (by a state or a value) is drawn whole in 3D (not only the timeline's shown span); the value's colour scale runs from its lowest to its highest along that track.
  • Sweeps: the Pareto levels are counted up to the tenth front; sets further back share level 11. With three or more objectives a Pareto chart shows two of them at a time (the front is the sets no other beats on all of them, so a front set can look beaten in one pair).
  • The tab's band of state lanes (the flight mode, inside the top plot or - Settings ▸ Look ▸ Mode band - above the plots) is shown when the tab's time plots are in one column with X linked; with several columns each plot keeps its own lane.
  • The faint copy of an object under the pointer on the map / in 3D follows time plots of the same tab only; the built-in Flight tab (map and 3D) has no time plot - add one to see it.
  • A template keeps its default tabs; a line's dash chosen by hand (Inspector ▸ Line) is kept in the session, not in templates.
  • In a segment comparison the difference view's times are since each segment's start: a click there does not move the cursor.
  • Golden runs and Compare's tolerances are kept in the app's settings and in the tolerances file (Save tolerances…), not in a session or a template. The Compare panel pairs signals by name: a tolerances file's "as" (another name in the run) is used by signalviewer-cli compare and kept when the panel saves the file.
  • Formulas keep a missing value missing (a sum, mean or norm in Create signals also offers to skip or bridge it; a formula does not yet).
  • The data-quality summary is of a file as it was opened or read again; a file growing in live mode is not checked again as it grows. A state or event signal (a mode, a message) is checked for missing values only.
  • The list of all events (modes, log events, findings, conditions, limits) is Checks ▸ Events of a flight log; for other files ] / [ and the command palette step through the conditions and limits.
  • Tacview export (.acmi): the objects only (not the plots' other signals), 10 samples a second, the whole recording; a recording whose times are not Unix clock seconds starts at 2000-01-01 00:00 UTC in Tacview; an object without its own roll (drawn from its motion) is level. The file is plain text (Tacview also reads it zipped).
  • Object guesses read names only: an object whose position signals do not share a prefix (lat, lon alone, or gpsLat with navLon) is offered through Advanced… rather than found; a motion attitude has no roll.
  • Local positions (NED / ENU): the origin is one point - the first valid sample of the origin signals. A PX4 origin that is reset during the flight (ref_timestamp) is not followed. A position in cm or mm is found but not added until it is converted to metres (ƒ); bare x / y / z with no frame word are not guessed (ROS pose.position). ArduPilot's lane quaternions (XKQ) are not paired with the lanes - their own roll / pitch / yaw are used.
  • Altitudes are compared as recorded: ArduPilot's POS / GPS / ORGN heights are above sea level, a position converted from ECEF is above the ellipsoid - comparing the two shows the geoid height (about 18 - 20 m in Israel) as a constant vertical error.
  • A map saved as HTML embeds the offline basemap for the tracks' area within about 15 MB (the file says which zoom levels it holds); online imagery is used only if it was on and already in the app's cache. The 3D view saves a PNG only.
  • Compare with similar… reads names of one file; the same signal across files is the Compare panel. One plot at a time is a way to look, not part of a session or a report.
  • The 3D camera On the object and the map's smoothness depend on the graphics: on software rendering (no GPU) the 3D view uses lighter settings.
  • Line styles: opacity is not a line setting (a setpoint's faded look is automatic).
  • The Map's flat drawing (where 3D cannot draw, or Always flat) has no terrain relief, sky, shadows, cockpit camera or error surface; the error is shown by colouring the compared track instead.
  • The offline 3D page draws the ground as a flat local plane (no earth curvature) - right for a flight of tens of kilometres, increasingly off beyond ~100 km.
  • MGRS covers 80° S to 84° N; near the poles (the UPS grid) positions are shown in decimal degrees.
  • Places: KML styles, folders and time spans are not imported (the shapes and names are); a polygon's holes are left out. Lines and areas are drawn 2 m over the ground in the light mode.
  • Statistics of the shown window and the at-a-glance mean are plain means of the samples, not weighted by time: where a signal's rate changes, its faster part counts more. The run at a glance holds at most four numbers per run.
  • Parameters ▸ Compare with compares two files at a time; a parameter changed during the run is compared by its first and last value.
  • My maps take raster tiles only (PNG / JPEG / WebP MBTiles, XYZ / TMS servers); vector (pbf) MBTiles and WMS are not read. Keep this area offline… is offered only where the map's terms allow bulk downloads (the ground heights and your own servers), not for OpenStreetMap, Esri or OpenTopoMap.
  • The height profile's ground is as fine as the heights the app has there (the bundled grids, .hgt files, kept areas); where it is coarse the profile says so.
  • Story mode picks at most 12 moments; the reference object's track gives the computed ones (the other objects only through the pair).

docs.title: The network
docs.text:
The map's default background, Offline, is the offline map the app draws from data it ships with: nothing is sent. The online backgrounds - marked ☁ in the Map background picker in the corner of every map (streets: OpenStreetMap or Esri; light / dark grey, satellite and Satellite + roads: Esri; topographic: OpenTopoMap) - are used only when you choose one (opening the picker downloads nothing: its pictures come from the tiles already on the disk); the app then requests the tiles of the area on screen from that provider - through its own server, so the page itself never talks to the internet - and keeps them in ~/.signalviewer/tiles. Such a request carries the tile's coordinates (roughly where you are looking) and the app's name. While online tiles are in use the plot shows an amber Online map sign.

Never use the network (Settings), or SV_OFFLINE=1 in the environment (it locks the setting on, for a whole installation): the online maps are greyed out in the picker with the reason, a session that chose one shows the offline map, and the server refuses every download (app/tiles.py checks it before any request) - tiles already on the disk are still shown. A map server of your own (My maps) on this PC or a private (local-network) address is not the internet and stays allowed; one on the internet is blocked. Nothing else in the app uses the network: the 3D view's terrain and imagery are the bundled ones (no Cesium ion), and there is no update check or telemetry.

docs.title: Offline map data
docs.text:
backend/app/basemap_data/ (17 MB) is built by python tools/make_basemap.py --all on a machine with internet (needs pyshp and osmium besides the app's libraries) and ships with the app: elevation grids (world ~11 km, Israel and surroundings ~500 m, Israel ~130 m) from the AWS "Terrain Tiles" (Mapzen / Tilezen: SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1), Natural Earth (public domain), and OpenStreetMap from Geofabrik extracts (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL). The app draws map tiles from them (backend/app/basemap.py, cached in ~/.signalviewer/tiles); the map shows the attribution. To refresh the data, run the tool again.

More detailed areas (packs). Any area can get the same detail as Israel: elevation (~130 m), OpenStreetMap roads down to regional ones, places down to villages, airports and runways:

python tools/make_basemap.py --pack cyprus --bbox 34.5,32.2,35.75,34.65 --countries europe/cyprus

--bbox is south,west,north,east; --countries the Geofabrik extracts covering it (comma-separated); --zoom 9 or 8 for coarser (smaller) elevation. The pack is written to backend/app/basemap_data/packs/<name>/ (pack.json, dem.npz, vectors.json.gz; ~1.4 MB for Cyprus) and the app uses every pack in that folder - copy a pack folder there on an offline machine.

Country borders. The offline map and the satellite photos get the borders and the country names from the app itself (Natural Earth 1:50m, simplified to about 3 km - good for seeing which country, not for a border's exact line): Borders, in the Map background picker. The street maps draw their own.

docs.title: My maps and keeping an area offline (1.27)
docs.text:
My maps (Map picker → Add a map…): a raster MBTiles file (read on this PC, fully offline) or a tile server of your own (XYZ, or TMS with its y axis flipped - for example a server on the local network). It is a background like any other, in 2D, 3D, exported pictures and offline map pages. The list lives in ~/.signalviewer/mymaps.json; Remove from My maps forgets one (the file or server is not touched).

Keep this area offline… (the same picker): before going to the field, download the tiles of the area on screen at the zooms you choose. The number of tiles and the size are estimated first; the download runs in the background with progress and Stop; the kept areas are listed with their size and Delete (a tile another kept area also covers stays). Only where the map's terms allow bulk downloads: the ground heights (open data) and your own servers. OpenStreetMap, Esri and OpenTopoMap forbid it - the dialog says so; the places you look at are still kept in the cache as before. The list lives in ~/.signalviewer/kept_areas.json.

docs.title: Height profile and arrows along the path (1.27)
docs.text:
Height profile (Profile under the map bar's ⋯): under the map, the object's height and the ground under it along the distance flown, for any recording with positions (/api/profile, the ground from the same heights as the 3D terrain). The cursor's moment is marked; a click in the profile moves the cursor. Where the ground data is coarse (outside the detailed areas) the profile says so and how to get finer ground: .hgt files (Settings → Map and objects, the folder of your elevation files) or Keep this area offline….

Arrows along the path (an object's settings): any two signals that are north and east components - a wind, a velocity, a force - drawn as arrows along the object's track, on the 2D map and in 3D. The file's own pair is offered by itself (an ArduPilot log's estimated wind, a CSV's north / east velocity).

docs.title: 3D view
docs.text:
CesiumJS (pinned, frontend/package.json) is loaded only when a plot is switched to 3D; its web workers and data files are copied into the UI build under /cesium/ (frontend/vite.config.ts), nothing comes from the internet. Terrain heights come from /api/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y} (the same bundled elevation grids as the offline map: sea at 0 m, the Jordan rift really below it). The object models are built by python tools/make_models.py into frontend/public/models/. Graphics: with a graphics card Cesium draws at the display's frame rate; drawn in software (virtual machines, remote desktop) it is slow - the app then uses one sample per pixel and less terrain detail (about 3x faster) and shows a note.

Outside the app (1.26, backend/app/scene3d.py): the 3D view in reports, the replay page and its own offline HTML file (its ⋯ menu; signalviewer-cli map --3d, sv.scene_html / sv.scene_image). CesiumJS cannot go into one file, so the page draws the same data with three.js r159 (MIT, embedded): the offline map draped on the bundled terrain (97 × 97 heights over the tracks' box and a margin), each track drawn as the app draws it (a fixed width on screen; a navigation solution dashed, a receiver as points), the app's models with heading, pitch and roll, heights ×1 / ×2 / ×5. The 2D map's page and the 3D page share one toolbar and one relation box (report_assets/relation.js, mappage.css, the words in mapimage.PAGE_STRINGS): the camera Free · On the object on a chosen object (as in the app: a drag turns around it, the wheel goes towards it down to sitting on it), + / −, Fit, Trail (whole / 60 s / 20 s), Relation (show / hide), light / dark; an attitude indicator in 3D; the address keeps the view (#t=…&cam=…&obj=…); Closest in moves the time (inside a report: the report's time, replay-seek); the box is the app's (range, horizontal, Δalt, bearing, relative bearing, closure, closest-in, heading Δ) with the pair's rings and a dashed line with the distance. The objects are read as the Tacview export reads them. Where the browser has no WebGL the page shows the scene's picture (matplotlib, the same picture as in PDF / Word / PNG). The scene is local east / north / up metres around the tracks' middle (a flat earth: fine for tracks of kilometres, not for hundreds of them).

docs.title: What is a position (P2, 1.26)
docs.text: One rule, in track_of (backend/app/routes/analysis.py, no_position_as_gap), used by every drawing and export: a sample whose latitude and longitude are both exactly 0, or outside ±90 / ±180, or not finite, is not a position - it is a gap. Receivers and autopilots write 0, 0 for "no fix" (ArduPilot's EAHR without an external AHRS: 0, 0 for the whole flight; a GPS before its first fix). Detection still goes by names; Add all and the found list then ask /api/object_positions and leave out an object with no position (the message names it), and note one with under 2 % positions. An object already in a saved session that turns out empty is drawn as nothing, left out of Fit and of every export, and its chip says no position. A latitude of 0 alone (a place on the equator) is a position.

docs.title: The ground's heights (P5, 1.26)
docs.text:
